en: The Haitian Revolution as a Non-event
zh: 作为非事件的海地革命

children: The young woman stood up in the middle of my lecture. “Mr. Trouillot, you make us read all those white scholars. What can they know about slavery? Where were they when we were jumping off the boats? When we chose death over misery and killed our own children to spare them from a life of rape?”
那位年轻女性在我的讲座中途站了起来。“特鲁约先生，您让我们读所有那些白人学者。他们对奴隶制能知道什么？当我们从船上跳下去的时候，他们在哪里？当我们宁死不愿受苦、杀死自己的孩子不让孩子一辈子受强暴时，他们在哪里？”

I was scared and she was wrong. She was not reading white authors only and she never jumped from a slave ship. I was dumbfounded and she was angry; but how does one reason with anger? I was on my way to a Ph.D., and my teaching this course was barely a stopover, a way of paying the dues of guilt in this lily-white institution. She had taken my class as a mental break on her way to med school, or Harvard law, or some lily-white corporation.
我很害怕，而她错了。她读的不只是白人作者，她也从未从奴隶船上跳下去过。我目瞪口呆，而她怒气冲冲；可是人如何与愤怒讲理？我当时正在攻读博士的路上，教这门课不过是一个中途站，一种在这所清一色由白人占据的学校里，因内疚而缴的一份会费。她选我的课，是在去医学院、哈佛法学院或某家清一色白人的公司的路上换换脑子。

I had entitled the course “The Black Experience in the Americas.” I should have known better: it attracted the few black students around—plus a few courageous whites—and they were all expecting too much, much more than I could deliver. They wanted a life that no narrative could provide, even the best fiction. They wanted a life that only they could build right now, right here in the United States—except that they did not know this: they were too close to the unfolding story. Yet already I could see in their eyes that part of my lesson registered. I wanted them to know that slavery did not happen only in Georgia and Mississippi. I wanted them to learn that the African connection was more complex and tortuous than they had ever imagined, that the U.S. monopoly on both blackness and racism was itself a racist plot. And she had broken the spell on her way to Harvard law. I was a novice and so was she, each of us struggling with the history we chose, each of us also fighting an imposed oblivion.

我给这门课起的名字是“美洲的黑人经验”。我本该更清楚：它吸引了周围为数不多的黑人学生——加上几个勇敢的白人——而他们的期望都太高，远远超出我所能给予的。他们想要一种任何叙述都无法提供的生活，即便是最好的虚构也不行。他们想要一种只有他们自己此时此地、就在美国才能建造的生活——只是他们不知道这一点：他们离正在展开的故事太近了。然而我已经能从他们的眼睛里看出，我的课有些地方她们听进去了。我想让他们知道，奴隶制不只发生在佐治亚和密西西比。我想让他们明白，与非洲的关联比他们想象的更复杂、更曲折，美国对黑人性和种族主义的双重垄断本身就是一个种族主义阴谋。而她在去哈佛法学院的路上打破了魔咒。我是新手，她也是，我们各自与自己选择的历史搏斗，也各自与一种强加的遗忘搏斗。

Ten years later, I was visiting another institution with a less prestigious clientele and more modest dreams when another young black woman, the same age but much more timid, caught me again by surprise. “I am tired,” she said, “to hear about this slavery stuff. Can we hear the story of the black millionaires?” Had times changed so fast, or were their different takes on slavery reflections of class differences?
十年后，我访问另一所机构，那里的学生出身不那么显赫，梦想也更朴素，另一位年轻黑人女性——同样的年纪，却怯生生得多——再次让我猝不及防。“我听够了，”她说，“这些奴隶制的事。我们能讲讲黑人百万富翁的故事吗？”是时代变得这么快，还是她们对奴隶制的不同看法反映了阶级差异？

I flashed back to the first woman clinging so tightly to that slave boat. I understood better why she wanted to jump, even once, on her way to Harvard law, med school, or wherever. Custodian of the future for an imprisoned race whose young males do not live long enough to have a past, she needed this narrative of resistance. Nietzsche was wrong: this was no extra baggage, but a necessity for the journey, and who was I to say that it was no better a past than a bunch of fake millionaires, or a medal of St. Henry and the crumbling walls of a decrepit palace?
我一下子回想起第一个女性，她如此紧紧地抓着那艘奴隶船。我更明白了她为什么想在去哈佛法学院、医学院或别的地方的路上，从那艘船上跳一次，哪怕只有一次。作为一个被囚禁种族的未来的保管人——这个种族的年轻男性活不到拥有一个过去的年纪——她需要这个抵抗的叙述。尼采错了：这不是多余的行李，而是旅程的必需品；我又凭什么说，这个过去并不比一群假百万富翁、或一枚圣亨利勋章加一座破败宫殿的残垣更好？

I wish I could shuffle the years and put both young women in the same room. We would have shared stories not yet in the archives. We would have read Ntozake Shange’s tale of a colored girl dreaming of Toussaint Louverture and the revolution that the world forgot. Then we would have returned to the planters’ journals, to econometric history and its industry of statistics, and none of us would be afraid of the numbers. Hard facts are no more frightening than darkness. You can play with them if you are with friends. They are scary only if you read them alone.
我真希望能把年份洗牌，把两位年轻女性放进同一个房间。我们会分享尚未进入档案的故事。我们会读恩托扎克·尚热的那个故事：一个有色人种女孩梦见杜桑·卢维杜尔和那场被世界遗忘的革命。然后我们会回到种植园主的日志，回到计量史学及其统计工业，我们谁都不会害怕数字。硬事实并不比黑暗更可怕。和朋友在一起，你可以把玩它们。只有独自阅读时，它们才吓人。

We all need histories that no history book can tell, but they are not in the classroom—not the history classrooms, anyway. They are in the lessons we learn at home, in poetry and childhood games, in what is left of history when we close the history books with their verifiable facts. Otherwise, why would a black woman born and raised in the richest country of the late twentieth century be more afraid to talk about slavery than a white planter in colonial Saint-Domingue just days before rebellious slaves knocked on his door?
我们都需要任何历史书都无法讲述的历史，但它们不在教室里——至少不在历史教室里。它们在我们于家中学到的教训里，在诗歌和童年游戏里，在我们合上那些带着可核实事实的历史书之后剩下的历史里。否则，为什么一个在二十世纪末最富有的国家出生长大的黑人女性，会比殖民地圣多明各的一个白人种植园主更害怕谈论奴隶制——而后者距离叛乱奴隶敲开他的家门只有几天？
This is a story for young black Americans who are still afraid of the dark. Although they are not alone, it may tell them why they feel they are.
这是一个献给仍然怕黑的年轻美国黑人的故事。虽然他们并不孤单，但它也许能告诉他们，为什么他们觉得自己是孤单的。

en: Unthinking a Chimera
zh: 把“幻象”逐出想象

en: In 1790, just a few months before the beginning of the insurrection that shook Saint-Domingue and brought about the revolutionary birth of independent Haiti, French colonist La Barre reassured his metropolitan wife of the peaceful state of life in the tropics. He wrote: “There is no movement among our Negroes.… They don’t even think of it. They are very tranquil and obedient. A revolt among them is impossible.” And again: “We have nothing to fear on the part of the Negroes; they are tranquil and obedient.” And again: “The Negroes are very obedient and always will be. We sleep with doors and windows wide open. Freedom for Negroes is a chimera.”
zh: 1790年，就在震动圣多明各、促成独立海地革命性诞生的那场起义开始前几个月，法国殖民者拉巴尔向他在本土的妻子保证热带生活的平静。他写道：“我们的黑人没有任何动静。……他们甚至想都不想。他们非常安静、顺从。他们中间不可能发生叛乱。”又说：“黑人方面我们无可畏惧；他们安静而顺从。”又说：“黑人非常顺从，而且永远会如此。我们睡觉时门窗大开。黑人的自由不过是一场幻梦。”

en: Historian Roger Dorsinville, who cites these words, notes that a few months later the most important slave insurrection in recorded history had reduced to insignificance such abstract arguments about Negro obedience. I am not so sure. When reality does not coincide with deeply held beliefs, human beings tend to phrase interpretations that force reality within the scope of these beliefs. They devise formulas to repress the unthinkable and to bring it back within the realm of accepted discourse.
zh: 引用这些话的历史学家罗歇·多尔桑维尔指出，几个月后，有记录以来最重要的奴隶起义就使这类关于黑人顺从的抽象论证变得无足轻重。我不那么确定。当现实与根深蒂固的信念不一致时，人类倾向于构造一些解释，把现实强行塞进这些信念的范围。他们设计公式来压制无法构想之事，把它重新带回公认话语的领域。

en: La Barre’s views were by no means unique. Witness this manager who constantly reassured his patrons in almost similar words: “I live tranquilly in the midst of them without a single thought of their uprising unless that was fomented by the whites themselves.”

There were doubts at times. But the planters’ practical precautions aimed at stemming individual actions or, at worst, a sudden riot. No one in Saint-Domingue or elsewhere worked out a plan of response to a general insurrection.
zh: 拉巴尔的看法绝非孤例。看看这位管家，他不断以几乎相同的措辞让他的主人们放心：“我平静地生活在他们中间，从未想过他们会起义，除非那是白人自己煽动的。”
有时也有疑虑。但种植园主的实际预防措施针对的是个别行动，至多是一场突发的骚乱。圣多明各或其他任何地方，都没有人制定过应对全面起义的方案。

en: Indeed, the contention that enslaved Africans and their descendants could not envision freedom—let alone formulate strategies for gaining and securing such freedom—was based not so much on empirical evidence as on an ontology, an implicit organization of the world and its inhabitants. Although by no means monolithic, this worldview was widely shared by whites in Europe and the Americas and by many non-white plantation owners as well. Although it left room for variations, none of these variations included the possibility of a revolutionary uprising in the slave plantations, let alone a successful one leading to the creation of an independent state.
zh: 的确，被奴役的非洲人及其后裔无法想象自由——更不用说制定获得并保障这种自由的战略——这一论断，与其说基于经验证据，不如说基于一种本体论，一种对世界及其居民的隐含划分和安排。这种世界观虽绝非铁板一块，却为欧洲和美洲的白人以及许多非白人种植园主广泛共享。尽管它留有变异的余地，这些变异中却没有一种包含奴隶种植园发生革命性起义的可能性，更不用说一场成功的、导致独立国家建立的起义。

en: The Haitian Revolution thus entered history with the peculiar characteristic of being unthinkable even as it happened. Official debates and publications of the times, including the long list of pamphlets on Saint-Domingue published in France from 1790 to 1804, reveal the incapacity of most contemporaries to understand the ongoing revolution on its own terms.
They could read the news only with their ready-made categories, and these categories were incompatible with the idea of a slave revolution.
zh: 于是，海地革命带着一个奇特的特征进入历史：它即使在发生之时也是无法构想的。当时的官方辩论和出版物，包括1790至1804年间在法国出版的关于圣多明各的一长串小册子，显示了大多数同时代人无法按这场正在进行的革命自身的逻辑来理解它。
他们只能用现成的范畴来阅读新闻，而这些范畴与奴隶革命的概念互不相容。

en: The discursive context within which news from Saint-Domingue was discussed as it happened has important consequences for the historiography of Saint-Domingue/Haiti. If some events cannot be accepted even as they occur, how can they be assessed later? In other words, can historical narratives convey plots that are unthinkable in the world within which these narratives take place? How does one write a history of the impossible?
zh: 当时的人用怎样的话语来理解圣多明各传来的消息，对圣多明各／海地的史学产生了深远影响。如果一些事件在发生之时都无法被接受，事后又如何评估它们？换句话说，历史叙述能否讲出这样一些情节：在这些叙述所处的世界里，它们根本无法构想？人如何书写一部不可能之事的历史？

en: The key issue is not ideological. Ideological treatments are now more current in Haiti itself (in the epic or bluntly political interpretations of the revolution favored by some Haitian writers) than in the more rigorous handling of the evidence by professionals in Europe or in North America. The international scholarship on the Haitian Revolution has been rather sound by modern standards of evidence since at least the 1940s. The issue is rather epistemological and, by inference, methodological in the broadest sense. Standards of evidence notwithstanding, to what extent has modern historiography of the Haitian Revolution—as part of a continuous Western discourse on slavery, race, and colonization—broken the iron bonds of the philosophical milieu in which it was born?
zh: 关键问题不是意识形态的。意识形态化的处理如今在海地本土（在一些海地作家偏爱的史诗式或直白政治化的革命解释中）比在欧洲或北美职业学者对证据更严格的处理中更为流行。至少自1940年代以来，关于海地革命的国际研究按现代证据标准衡量已相当扎实。问题毋宁说是认识论的，并由此推及最广义的方法论。尽管有证据标准，作为关于奴隶制、种族和殖民的连续西方话语的一部分，现代海地革命史学在多大程度上打破了它诞生于其中的哲学环境的铁箍？

en: A Certain Idea of Man
zh: 某种关于人的观念

en: The West was created somewhere at the beginning of the sixteenth century in the midst of a global wave of material and symbolic transformations. The definitive expulsion of the Muslims from Europe, the so-called voyages of exploration, the first developments of merchant colonialism, and the maturation of the absolutist state set the stage for the rulers and merchants of Western Christendom to conquer Europe and the rest of the world. This historical itinerary was political, as evidenced by the now well-known names that it evokes—Columbus, Magellan, Charles V, the Hapsburgs, and the turning moments that set its pace—the reconquest of Castile and of Aragon, the laws of Burgos, the transmission of papal power from the Borgias to the Medicis.
zh: 西方是在十六世纪初叶，在一场全球性的物质与象征转型浪潮中被创造出来的。穆斯林被最终逐出欧洲、所谓的探索航行、商业殖民主义的最初发展、绝对主义国家的成熟，为西方基督教世界的统治者和商人征服欧洲及世界其余地方搭建了舞台。这一历史行程是政治性的，它所唤起的那些如今广为人知的名字就是明证——哥伦布、麦哲伦、查理五世、哈布斯堡家族，以及为它定步调的那些转折时刻——卡斯蒂利亚和阿拉贡的再征服、布尔戈斯诸法、教皇权力从博尔贾家族向美第奇家族的转移。

en: These political developments paralleled the emergence of a new symbolic order. The invention of the Americas (with Waldseemuller, Vespucci, and Balboa), the simultaneous invention of Europe, the division of the Mediterranean by an imaginary line going from the south of Cadiz to the north of Constantinople, the westernization of Christianity, and the invention of a Greco-Roman past to Western Europe were all part of the process through which Europe became the West.

What we call the Renaissance, much more an invention in its own right than a rebirth, ushered in a number of philosophical questions to which politicians, theologians, artists, and soldiers provided both concrete and abstract answers. What is Beauty? What is Order? What is the State? But also and above all: What is Man?
zh: 这些政治发展伴随着一种新象征秩序的出现。美洲的发明（与瓦尔德泽米勒、韦斯普奇和巴尔沃亚一起）、欧洲的同时发明、用一条从加的斯以南到君士坦丁堡以北的想象线对地中海的划分、基督教的西方化、为西欧发明一个希腊—罗马的过去，都是欧洲借以成为西方的那个过程的一部分。
我们所谓的文艺复兴，与其说是再生，不如说本身就是一种发明，它引入了一系列哲学问题，政治家、神学家、艺术家和军人为这些问题提供了具体和抽象的回答。什么是美？什么是秩序？什么是国家？但还有、而且首要的是：什么是人？

en: Philosophers who discussed that last issue could not escape the fact that colonization was going on as they spoke. Men (Europeans) were conquering, killing, dominating, and enslaving other beings thought to be equally human, if only by some. The contest between Bartolomé de Las Casas and Juan Ginés de Sepúlveda at Valladolid on the nature and fate of the Indians in 1550–1551 was only one instance of this continuous encounter between the symbolic and the practical. Whence, the very ambiguities of the early Las Casas who believed both in colonization and in the humanity of the Indians and found it impossible to reconcile the two. But despite Las Casas and others, the Renaissance did not—could not—settle the question of the ontological nature of conquered peoples. As we well know, Las Casas himself offered a poor and ambiguous compromise that he was to regret later: freedom for the savages (the Indians), slavery for the barbarians (the Africans). Colonization won the day.
zh: 讨论最后那个问题的哲学家无法回避一个事实：他们说话之时，殖民正在进行。人（欧洲人）正在征服、杀戮、支配和奴役其他存在者，后者被认为同样是人类——尽管只被一些人这样认为。1550–1551年巴托洛梅·德·拉斯·卡萨斯与胡安·希内斯·德·塞普尔韦达在巴利亚多利德就印第安人的本性与命运进行的论战，只是象征与实践这种持续相遇的一个实例。由此就有了早期拉斯·卡萨斯的种种含混：他既相信殖民，又相信印第安人的人性，却发现两者无法调和。但尽管有拉斯·卡萨斯和其他人，文艺复兴没有——也不能——解决被征服民族的本体论本性问题。众所周知，拉斯·卡萨斯本人提出了一个糟糕而含混的妥协，他后来为之后悔：给野蛮人（savages，印第安人）自由，给蛮族（barbarians，非洲人）奴隶制。殖民占了上风。

en: The seventeenth century saw the increased involvement of England, France, and the Netherlands in the Americas and in the slave trade. The eighteenth century followed the same path with a touch of perversity: the more European merchants and mercenaries bought and conquered other men and women, the more European philosophers wrote and talked about Man. Viewed from outside the West, with its extraordinary increase in both philosophical musings and concrete attention to colonial practice, the century of the Enlightenment was also a century of confusion. There is no single view of blacks—or of any non-white group, for that matter—even within discrete European populations. Rather, non-European groups were forced to enter into various philosophical, ideological, and practical schemes. Most important for our purposes is that all these schemes recognized degrees of humanity. Whether these connecting ladders ranked chunks of humanity on ontological, ethical, political, scientific, cultural, or simply pragmatic grounds, the fact is that all assumed and reasserted that, ultimately, some humans were more so than others.
zh: 十七世纪见证了英国、法国和荷兰在美洲及奴隶贸易中日益加深的卷入。十八世纪沿着同一条路走下去，还带着一丝悖谬：欧洲商人和雇佣兵购买和征服的其他男女越多，欧洲哲学家就越是著书立说、谈论“人”。从西方之外看去，这个启蒙的世纪既是哲学沉思空前增多的世纪，也是对殖民实践具体关注空前增多的世纪，因而也是一个混乱的世纪。即便在各自独立的欧洲人群内部，对黑人——就此而言对任何非白人群体——也没有单一的看法。毋宁说，非欧洲群体被迫进入各种哲学的、意识形态的和实践的方案。对我们的目的来说最重要的是，所有这些方案都承认人性的等级。无论这些衔接的阶梯是按本体论的、伦理的、政治的、科学的、文化的还是纯粹实用的依据来给各类人群划分等级，事实是它们都假定并重申：归根结底，有些人比另一些人更是人。

en: For indeed, in the horizon of the West at the end of the century, Man (with a capital M) was primarily European and male. On this single point everyone who mattered agreed. Men were also, to a lesser degree, females of European origins, like the French “citoyennes,” or ambiguous whites, such as European Jews. Further down were peoples tied to strong state structures: Chinese, Persians, Egyptians, who exerted a different fascination on some Europeans for being at the same time more “advanced” and yet potentially more evil than other Westerners. On reflection, and only for a timid minority, Man could also be westernized man, the complacent colonized. The benefit of doubt did not extend very far: westernized (or more properly, “westernizable”) humans, natives of Africa or of the Americas, were at the lowest level of this nomenclature.
zh: 因为在世纪末西方的视野中，人（大写的 Man）首先是欧洲人和男性。在这一点上，所有要紧的人物都一致。其次，人也在较低程度上包括欧洲出身的女性，如法国的“女公民”（citoyennes），或含混的白人，如欧洲犹太人。再往下是与强大国家结构相连的民族：中国人、波斯人、埃及人，他们对一些欧洲人产生另一种魅力，因为他们同时比其他西方人更“先进”、却又可能更邪恶。再考虑一下，而且只对一小撮怯懦的少数人而言，人也可以是西化了的人，即安于被殖民处境的人。存疑从宽的待遇延伸不了多远：西化的（或更准确地说，“可西化的”）人类，非洲或美洲的土著，处于这一命名体系的最底层。

en: Negative connotations linked to skin colors increasingly regrouped as “black” had first spread in Christendom in the late Middle Ages. They were reinforced by the fanciful descriptions of medieval geographers and travellers. Thus, the word “nègre” entered French dictionaries and glossaries with negative undertones increasingly precise from its first appearances in the 1670s to the universal dictionaries that augured the Encyclopedia.
By the middle of the eighteenth century, “black” was almost universally bad. What had happened in the meantime, was the expansion of African-American slavery.
zh: 与日益被归并为“黑”的肤色相连的负面含义，最早在中世纪晚期的基督教世界传播开来。中世纪地理学家和旅行家的异想天开的描述强化了这些含义。于是，“nègre”一词进入法语词典和词汇表，从1670年代首次出现到预示《百科全书》的那些通用词典，其负面含义日益明确。
到十八世纪中叶，“黑”几乎普遍是坏的。在此期间发生的，是美洲非洲裔奴隶制的扩张。

en: Indeed, the rather abstract nomenclature inherited from the Renaissance was altogether reproduced, reinforced, and challenged by colonial practice and the philosophical literature. That is, eighteenth-century colonial practice brought to the fore both the certitudes and the ambiguities of the ontological order that paralleled the rise of the West.
zh: 的确，从文艺复兴继承来的那套相当抽象的命名体系，被殖民实践和哲学文献整个地再生产、强化和挑战。也就是说，十八世纪的殖民实践把与西方崛起相伴的本体论秩序的确定性与含混性都推到了前台。

en: Colonization provided the most potent impetus for the transformation of European ethnocentrism into scientific racism. In the early 1700s, the ideological rationalization of Afro-American slavery relied increasingly on explicit formulations of the ontological order inherited from the Renaissance. But in so doing, it also transformed the Renaissance worldview by bringing its purported inequalities much closer to the very practices that confirmed them. Blacks were inferior and therefore enslaved; black slaves behaved badly and were therefore inferior. In short, the practice of slavery in the Americas secured the blacks’ position at the bottom of the human world.
zh: 殖民为欧洲族群中心主义向科学种族主义的转变提供了最强大的动力。1700年代初，为美洲非洲裔奴隶制辩护的意识形态论证，越来越依赖对从文艺复兴继承的本体论秩序的明确表述。但这样做时，它也改变了文艺复兴的世界观，使其所谓的不平等更接近那些证实这些不平等的实践本身。黑人是低劣的，因此被奴役；黑人奴隶行为恶劣，因此是低劣的。简言之，美洲的奴隶制实践确保了黑人在人类世界底部的位置。

en: With the place of blacks now guaranteed at the bottom of the Western nomenclature, anti-black racism soon became the central element of planter ideology in the Caribbean. By the middle of the eighteenth century, the arguments justifying slavery in the Antilles and North America relocated in Europe where they blended with the racist strain inherent in eighteenth-century rationalist thought. The literature in French is telling, though by no means unique. Buffon fervently supported a monogenist viewpoint: blacks were not, in his view, of a different species. Still, they were different enough to be destined to slavery. Voltaire disagreed, but only in part. Negroes belonged to a different species, one culturally destined to be slaves. That the material well-being of many of these thinkers was often indirectly and, sometimes, quite directly linked to the exploitation of African slave labor may not have been irrelevant to their learned opinions. By the time of the American Revolution, scientific racism, whose rise many historians wrongly attribute to the nineteenth century, was already a feature of the ideological landscape of the Enlightenment on both sides of the Atlantic.
zh: 黑人在西方命名体系底部的位置如今有了保证，反黑人种族主义很快成为加勒比种植园主意识形态的核心要素。到十八世纪中叶，为安的列斯和北美奴隶制辩护的论证迁移到欧洲，在那里与十八世纪理性主义思想固有的种族主义脉络融合。法语文献很说明问题，尽管绝非孤例。布封热烈支持单源论观点：在他看来，黑人并非不同的物种。然而，他们的差异仍足以使其注定为奴。伏尔泰不同意，但只不同意一部分。黑人属于另一个物种，一个在文化上注定为奴的物种。这些思想家中许多人的物质福利往往间接、有时相当直接地与对非洲奴隶劳动的剥削相连，这对他们的博学见解也许并非无关。到美国革命之时，科学种族主义——许多历史学家错误地把它的兴起归于十九世纪——已经是大西洋两岸启蒙意识形态景观的一个特征。

en: Thus the Enlightenment exacerbated the fundamental ambiguity that dominated the encounter between ontological discourse and colonial practice. If the philosophers did reformulate some of the answers inherited from the Renaissance, the question “What is Man?” kept stumbling against the practices of domination and of merchant accumulation. The gap between abstraction and practice grew or, better said, the handling of the contradictions between the two became much more sophisticated, in part because philosophy provided as many answers as colonial practice itself. The Age of the Enlightenment was an age in which the slave drivers of Nantes bought titles of nobility to better parade with philosophers, an age in which a freedom fighter such as Thomas Jefferson owned slaves without bursting under the weight of his intellectual and moral contradictions.
zh: 于是，启蒙加剧了支配本体论话语与殖民实践之相遇的那种根本含混。如果说哲学家确实重新表述了从文艺复兴继承的某些答案，“什么是人？”这个问题却不断在支配与商业积累的实践上碰壁。抽象与实践之间的鸿沟扩大了，或者更准确地说，对两者之间矛盾的处理变得老练得多，部分原因在于哲学提供的答案与殖民实践本身一样多。启蒙时代是这样一个时代：南特的奴隶贩子购买贵族头衔，以便更好地与哲学家们一同招摇；也是这样一个时代：托马斯·杰斐逊这样的自由斗士拥有奴隶，却不会被自己智识与道德矛盾的重负压垮。

en: In the name of freedom and democracy also, in July 1789, just a few days before the storming of the Bastille, a few planters from Saint-Domingue met in Paris to petition the newly formed French Assembly to accept in its midst twenty representatives from the Caribbean. The planters had derived this number from the population of the islands, using roughly the mathematics used in France to proportion metropolitan representatives in the Assembly. But they had quite advertently counted the black slaves and the

as part of the population of the islands whereas, of course, they were claiming no rights of suffrage for these non-whites. Honoré Gabriel Riquetti, Count of Mirabeau, took the stand to denounce the planters’ skewed mathematics. Mirabeau told the Assembly:
zh: 同样以自由和民主的名义，1789年7月，就在攻占巴士底狱前几天，几位来自圣多明各的种植园主在巴黎集会，请愿新成立的法国议会接受二十名来自加勒比的代表进入它的行列。种植园主们从各岛人口推出这个数字，大致使用了法国用来按比例分配议会中本土代表的算法。但他们相当有意地把黑人奴隶和
算作各岛人口的一部分，而他们当然并不为这些非白人要求任何选举权。奥诺雷·加布里埃尔·里凯蒂，米拉波伯爵，登台谴责种植园主们歪曲的算法。米拉波对议会说：

en: Are the colonies placing their Negroes and their
in the class of men or in that of the beasts of burden?
zh: 各殖民地是把它们的黑人和
归入人的类别，还是归入驮畜的类别？

en: If the Colonists want the Negroes and

to count as men, let them enfranchise the first; that all may be electors, that all may be elected. If not, we beg them to observe that in proportioning the number of deputies to the population of France, we have taken into consideration neither the number of our horses nor that of our mules.
zh: 如果殖民者想让黑人和
算作人，就让他们先给黑人奴隶自由；要让两类人都享有选举权和被选举权。否则，我们请他们注意：在按法国人口比例确定代表人数时，我们既没有考虑我们的马匹数量，也没有考虑我们的骡子数量。

en: Mirabeau wanted the French Assembly to reconcile the philosophical positions explicit in the Declaration of Rights of Man and its political stance on the colonies. But the declaration spoke of “the Rights of Man and Citizen,” a title which denotes, as Tzvetan Todorov reminds us, the germ of a contradiction.

In this case the citizen won over the man—at least over the non-white man. The National Assembly granted only six deputies to the sugar colonies of the Caribbean, a few more than they deserved if only the whites had been counted but many less than if the Assembly had recognized the full political rights of the blacks and the
In the mathematics of realpolitik, the half-million slaves of Saint Domingue-Haiti and the few hundred thousands of the other colonies were apparently worth three deputies—white ones at that.
zh: 米拉波希望法国议会把《人权宣言》中明确的哲学立场与其在殖民地问题上的政治姿态调和起来。但宣言说的是“人与公民的权利”，正如茨维坦·托多罗夫提醒我们的，这个标题本身就包含矛盾的萌芽。
在这件事上，以公民资格衡量的权利压倒了作为人的权利，至少对于非白人如此。国民议会只给加勒比的蔗糖殖民地六个代表席位，如果只算白人，这比它们应得的还多几个；但如果议会承认黑人和
的完整政治权利，这就少得多了。在现实政治的算法中，圣多明各-海地的五十万奴隶和其他殖民地的几十万奴隶，显然只值三个代表——而且是白人代表。

en: The ease with which the Assembly bypassed its own contradictions, an echo of the mechanisms by which black slaves came to account for three-fifths of a person in the United States, permeated the practices of the Enlightenment. Jacques Thibau doubts that contemporaries found a dichotomy between the France of the slavers and that of the philosophers. “Was not the Western, maritime France, an integral part of France of the Enlightenment?”

Louis Sala-Molins further suggests that we distinguish between the advocacy of slavery and the racism of the time: one could oppose the first (on practical grounds) and not the other (on philosophical ones). Voltaire, notably, was racist, but often opposed slavery on practical rather than moral grounds. So did David Hume, not because he believed in the equality of blacks, but because, like Adam Smith, he considered the whole business too expensive. Indeed, in France as in England, the arguments for or against slavery in formal political arenas were more often than not couched in pragmatic terms, notwithstanding the mass appeal of British abolitionism and its religious connotations.
zh: 在启蒙时代的实践中，像议会这样轻易绕过自身矛盾的情况随处可见。美国把黑人奴隶按五分之三个人计算的做法与此遥相呼应。雅克·蒂博怀疑同时代人是否在奴隶贩子的法国与哲学家的法国之间看到二分。“西部的、沿海的法国，难道不是启蒙法国的一个组成部分吗？”

路易·萨拉-莫兰进一步建议我们区分对奴隶制的拥护与当时的种族主义：一个人可以（基于实际理由）反对前者，却不（基于哲学理由）反对后者。尤其值得注意的是，伏尔泰是种族主义者，却常常基于实际而非道德理由反对奴隶制。大卫·休谟也是如此，不是因为他相信黑人平等，而是因为他和亚当·斯密一样，认为整桩生意太贵。的确，在法国和英国一样，正式政治舞台上赞成或反对奴隶制的论证，大多以实用措辞表述，尽管英国废奴主义有大众号召力及其宗教内涵。

en: The Enlightenment, nevertheless, brought a change of perspective. The idea of progress, now confirmed, suggested that men were perfectible. Therefore, subhumans could be, theoretically at least, perfectible. More important, the slave trade was running its course, and the economics of slavery would be questioned increasingly as the century neared its end. Perfectibility became an argument in the practical debate: the westernized other looked increasingly more profitable to the West, especially if he could become a free laborer. A French memoir of 1790 summarized the issue: “It is perhaps not impossible to civilize the Negro, to bring him to principles and

children: make a man out of him

en: : there would be more to gain than to buy and sell him.” Finally, we should not underestimate the loud anti-colonialist stance of a small, elitist but vocal group of philosophers and politicians.
zh: 不过，启蒙带来了视角的变化。如今得到确认的进步观念提示，人是可完善的。因此，次等人至少在理论上也可以是可完善的。更重要的是，奴隶贸易正走向尽头，随着世纪接近尾声，奴隶制的经济学将越来越多地受到质疑。可完善性成了实际辩论中的一个论据：西化的他者对西方来说显得越来越有利可图，尤其是如果他能成为自由劳动者。1790年的一份法国论稿概括了这个问题：“开化黑人也许并非不可能，让他懂得准则、
：这比买卖他更有利可图。”最后，我们不应低估一小群精英主义但声音响亮的哲学家和政治家的高调反殖民立场。

en: The reservations expressed in the metropolis had little impact within the Caribbean or in Africa. Indeed, the slave trade increased in the years 1789–1791 while French politicians and philosophers were debating more vehemently than ever on the rights of humanity. Further, few politicians or philosophers attacked racism, colonialism, and slavery in a single blow and with equal vehemence. In France as in England colonialism, pro-slavery rhetoric, and racism intermingled and supported one another without ever becoming totally confused. So did their opposites. That allowed much room for multiple positions.
zh: 本土表达的保留意见在加勒比或非洲内部影响甚微。的确，1789–1791年间，当法国政治家和哲学家比以往更激烈地辩论人类权利时，奴隶贸易却增加了。再者，很少有政治家或哲学家以同等的激烈程度一举攻击种族主义、殖民主义和奴隶制。在法国和英国一样，殖民主义、拥奴修辞和种族主义相互交织、相互支持，却从未完全混为一谈。它们的对立面也是如此。这为多重立场留下了很大空间。

en: Such multiplicity notwithstanding, there was no doubt about Western superiority, only about its proper use and effect.

, signed by Abbé Raynal with philosopher and encyclopedist Denis Diderot acting as ghost—and, some would say, premier—contributor to the anti-colonialist passages, was perhaps the most radical critique of colonialism from the France of the Enlightenment.

Yet the book never fully questioned the ontological principles behind the colonialist enterprise, namely that the differences between forms of humanity were not only of degree but of kind, not historical but primordial. The polyphony of the book further limited its anti-slavery impact.
Bonnet rightly points that the
is a book that reveres at once the immobile vision of the noble savage and the benefits of industry and human activity.
zh: 尽管有这种多重性，对西方的优越性却无人怀疑，有疑问的只是它的恰当运用和效果。
署名雷纳尔神父，哲学家兼百科全书派德尼·狄德罗为反殖民段落捉刀——有人会说，他是首要撰稿人——它也许是启蒙法国最激进的殖民主义批判。
然而这本书从未彻底质疑殖民事业背后的本体论原则，即各种被界定为“人”的群体之间的差异不仅是程度上的，而且是种类上的，不是历史的而是原初的。这本书的多声部进一步限制了它的反奴隶制影响。
博内正确地指出，
是一本同时尊崇高贵的野蛮人那静止不变的图景与工业和人类活动之益处的书。

en: Behind the radicalism of Diderot and Raynal stood, ultimately, a project of colonial management. It did indeed include the abolition of slavery, but only in the long term, and as part of a process that aimed at the better control of the colonies.
Access to human status did not lead
to self-determination. In short, here again, as in Condorcet, as in Mirabeau, as in Jefferson, when all is said and done, there are degrees of humanity.
zh: 在狄德罗和雷纳尔的激进主义背后，最终站着一个殖民管理方案。它确实包括废除奴隶制，但只在长期意义上，而且作为一个旨在更好控制殖民地的过程的一部分。
获得人的地位并不
导致自决。简言之，这里再一次，如同在孔多塞那里、在米拉波那里、在杰斐逊那里，说千道万，人性是有等级的。

en: The vocabulary of the times reveals that gradation. When one talked of the biological product of black and of white intercourse, one spoke of “man of color” as if the two terms do not necessarily go together: unmarked humanity is white. The captain of a slave boat bluntly emphasized this implicit opposition between white “Men” and the rest of humankind. After French supporters of the free coloreds in Paris created the
, the pro-slavery captain proudly labelled himself “l’Ami des Hommes.” The Friends of the Blacks were not necessarily Friends of Man.

The lexical opposition Man-versus-Native (or Man-versus-Negro) tinted the European literature on the Americas from 1492 to the Haitian Revolution and beyond. Even the radical duo Diderot-Raynal did not escape it. Recounting an early Spanish exploration, they write: “Was not this handful of
surrounded by an innumerable multitude of
… seized with alarm and terror, well or ill founded?”
zh: 当时的词汇揭示了那种等级。当人们谈到黑人与白人交合的生物学产物时，说的是“有色人”（man of color），仿佛这两个词并不必然连在一起：无标记的人性是白的。一艘奴隶船的船长直白地强调了白人“人”与人类其余部分之间的这种隐性对立。在巴黎支持自由有色人的法国人创立

children: 黑人之友社（Société des Amis des Noirs）

zh: 之后，这位拥奴船长自豪地自称“人类之友”（l’Ami des Hommes）。黑人之友未必是人类之友。
“人”与“土著”（或“人”与“黑人”）在用词上的对立，染遍了从1492年到海地革命乃至其后的欧洲美洲文献。连激进的狄德罗—雷纳尔二人组也未能免俗。在记述一次早期西班牙探险时，他们写道：“这一小撮
被无数
包围……难道不会惊慌恐惧吗，无论这恐惧有无根据？”

en: One will not castigate long-dead writers for using the words of their time or for not sharing ideological views that we now take for granted. Lest accusations of political correctness trivialize the issue, let me emphasize that I am not suggesting that eighteenth-century men and women
have thought about the fundamental equality of humankind in the same way some of us do today. On the contrary, I am arguing that they

have done so. But I am also drawing a lesson from the understanding of this historical impossibility. The Haitian Revolution did challenge the ontological and political assumptions of the most radical writers of the Enlightenment.

children: The events that shook up Saint-Domingue from 1791 to 1804 constituted a sequence for which not even the extreme political left in France or in England had a conceptual frame of reference.

en: They were “unthinkable” facts in the framework of Western thought.
zh: 人们不会因早已作古的作家使用他们时代的词语、或不持有我们如今视为当然的意识形态观点而苛责他们。为避免政治正确的指责把问题琐碎化，让我强调：我不是在说十八世纪的男女
像我们今天的一些人那样思考人类的根本平等。恰恰相反，我的论点是：他们
那样做。但我也从对这种历史不可能性的理解中吸取一个教训。海地革命确实挑战了启蒙最激进作家的本体论和政治预设。

children: 1791至1804年震动圣多明各的那些事件构成一个序列，对此连法国或英国最极端的政治左派都没有一个概念参照框架。

zh: 在西方思想的框架中，它们是“无法构想的”事实。

en: Pierre Bourdieu defines the unthinkable as that for which one has no adequate instruments to conceptualize. He writes: “In the unthinkable of an epoch, there is all that one cannot think for want of ethical or political inclinations that predispose to take it in account or in consideration, but also that which one cannot think for want of instruments of thought such as problematics, concepts, methods, techniques.”

The unthinkable is that which one cannot conceive within the range of possible alternatives, that which perverts all answers because it defies the terms under which the questions were phrased. In that sense, the Haitian Revolution was unthinkable in its time: it challenged the very framework within which proponents and opponents had examined race, colonialism, and slavery in the Americas.
zh: 皮埃尔·布尔迪厄把无法构想之事定义为人们没有适当工具加以概念化的东西。他写道：“在一个时代的无法构想之事中，有一切因缺乏伦理或政治倾向——这些倾向使人预先倾向于把它纳入考量——而无法思考的东西，也有因缺乏问题式、概念、方法、技术等思想工具而无法思考的东西。”
无法构想之事，是人们在可能选项的范围内无法设想的东西，是使一切答案都失效的东西，因为它拒斥问题被提出时所依据的那些条件。在这个意义上，海地革命在其时代是无法构想的：它挑战了支持者和反对者借以考察美洲种族、殖民主义和奴隶制的那个框架本身。

en: Prelude to the News: The Failure of Categories
zh: 新闻的序曲：范畴的失效

en: Between the first slave shipments of the early 1500s and the 1791 insurrection of northern Saint-Domingue, most Western observers had treated manifestations of slave resistance and defiance with the ambivalence characteristic of their overall treatment of colonization and slavery. On the one hand, resistance and defiance did not exist, since to acknowledge them was to acknowledge the humanity of the enslaved.

On the other hand, since resistance occurred, it was dealt with quite severely, within or around the plantations. Thus, next to a discourse that claimed the contentment of slaves, a plethora of laws, advice, and measures, both legal and illegal, were set up to curb the very resistance denied in theory.
zh: 从16世纪初最早的奴隶贩运到1791年圣多明各北部的起义，大多数西方观察家都以一种矛盾心态对待奴隶抵抗与反抗的种种表现，这种矛盾心态正是他们总体对待殖民与奴隶制的特征。一方面，抵抗与反抗并不存在，因为承认它们就等于承认被奴役者的人性。
另一方面，既然抵抗确实发生，就在种植园内部或其周边遭到相当严厉的处置。于是，在宣称奴隶心满意足的话语旁边，又设置了大量法律、忠告和措施——合法的和非法的——来遏制那种在理论上被否认的抵抗。

en: Publications by and for planters, as well as plantation journals and correspondence, often mixed both attitudes. Close as some were to the real world, planters and managers could not fully deny resistance, but they tried to provide reassuring certitudes by trivializing all its manifestations. Resistance did not exist as a global phenomenon. Rather, each case of unmistakable defiance, each possible instance of resistance was treated separately and drained of its political content. Slave A ran away because he was particularly mistreated by his master. Slave B was missing because he was not properly fed. Slave X killed herself in a fatal tantrum. Slave Y poisoned her mistress because she was jealous. The runaway emerges from this literature—which still has its disciples—as an animal driven by biological constraints, at best as a pathological case. The rebellious slave in turn is a maladjusted Negro, a mutinous adolescent who eats dirt until he dies, an infanticidal mother, a deviant. To the extent that sins of humanity are acknowledged they are acknowledged only as evidence of a pathology.
zh: 种植园主自己撰写、面向种植园主的出版物，以及种植园日志和通信，常常把两种态度混在一起。尽管其中一些人与现实世界贴得很近，种植园主和管理者无法完全否认抵抗，但他们试图通过把抵抗的一切表现琐碎化，来提供令人安心的确定性。抵抗并不作为一种整体现象存在。毋宁说，每一桩确凿的反抗、每一个可能的抵抗事例都被单独处理，并被抽干其政治内容。奴隶甲逃跑，因为他受到主人的特别虐待。奴隶乙失踪，因为他没吃饱。奴隶丙在一场致命的暴怒中自杀。奴隶丁毒死女主人，因为她嫉妒。在这种文献——它至今仍有门徒——中，逃亡者呈现为受生物性约束驱使的动物，至多是一个病理学个案。反叛的奴隶则是一个适应不良的黑人，一个吃土直到吃死的叛逆少年，一个杀婴的母亲，一个越轨者。即便他们承认这些是人会犯的过错，也只把它们当作病态的证据。

en: In retrospect, this argument is not very convincing to anyone aware of the infinite spectrum of human reactions to forms of domination. It is at best an anemic caricature of methodological individualism. Would each single explanation be true, the sum of all of them would say little of the causes and effects of the repetition of such cases.
zh: 事后看来，对任何了解人类面对各种支配形式时反应之无限光谱的人来说，这套论证都不大有说服力。它至多是方法论个体主义的一幅贫血的漫画。即便每一个单独的解释都为真，把它们全部加起来，对于这些事例反复出现的原因与后果，也说不出什么。

en: In fact, this argument didn’t convince the planters themselves. They held on to it because it was the only scheme that allowed them not to deal with the issue as a mass phenomenon. That latter interpretation was inconceivable. Built into any system of domination is the tendency to proclaim its own normalcy. To acknowledge resistance as a mass phenomenon is to acknowledge the possibility that something is wrong with the system. Caribbean planters, much as their counterparts in Brazil and in the United States, systematically rejected that ideological concession, and their arguments in defense of slavery were central to the development of scientific racism.
zh: 事实上，这套论证连种植园主自己都没说服。他们抓住它不放，因为它是唯一能让他们不必把这个问题当作群体现象来处理的图式。后一种解释是不可想象的。任何支配系统都内建了一种倾向：宣称自身的常态性。把抵抗承认为群体现象，就是承认系统可能出了毛病。加勒比的种植园主，正如他们在巴西和美国的同行一样，系统地拒绝这一意识形态让步；他们为奴隶制辩护的论证，在科学种族主义的发展中居于核心地位。

en: Yet, as time went on, the succession of plantation revolts, and especially the consolidation—in Jamaica, and in the Guianas—of large colonies of runaways with whom colonial governments had to negotiate, gradually undermined the image of submission and the complementary argument of pathological misadaptation. However much some observers wanted to see in these massive departures a sign of the force that nature exerted on the animal-slave, the possibility of mass resistance penetrated Western discourse.
zh: 然而，随着时间推移，种植园起义接连不断，尤其是在牙买加和圭亚那地区，大型逃亡奴隶聚居地日益巩固，迫使殖民政府同它们谈判。这逐渐瓦解了顺从的形象以及病理性适应不良这一配套论证。无论某些观察家多么想在这些大规模出走中看到自然施加于动物—奴隶的力量之标志，群体抵抗的可能性还是渗入了西方话语。

en: The penetration was nevertheless circumspect. When Louis-Sébastien Mercier announced an avenger of the New World in 1771, it was in a novel of anticipation, a utopia.

The goal was to warn Europeans of the fatalities that awaited them if they did not change their ways. Similarly, when the duo Raynal-Diderot spoke of a black Spartacus, it was not a clear prediction of a Louverture-type character, as some would want with hindsight.
In the pages of the

where the passage appears, the threat of a black Spartacus is couched as a warning. The reference is not to Saint-Domingue but to Jamaica and to Guyana where “there are two established colonies of fugitive negroes.… These flashes of lightning announce the thunder, and the negroes lack only a chief courageous enough to drive them to
Where is he, this great man whom nature owes
to the honor of the human species? Where is this new Spartacus?…”
zh: 然而这种渗透是谨慎的。1771年，路易-塞巴斯蒂安·梅西耶宣告一位新世界的复仇者时，那是在一部设想未来的小说、一部乌托邦之中。
目的是警告欧洲人：若不改变行事方式，等待他们的将是怎样的灭顶之灾。同样，当雷纳尔—狄德罗二人谈到一位黑人斯巴达克斯时，那并不是对卢维杜尔式人物的明确预言，尽管有人事后想把它说成是。
在
出现这段话的那些页里，黑人斯巴达克斯的威胁是以警告的口吻表述的。所指不是圣多明各，而是牙买加和圭亚那，那里“有两个已经立足的逃亡黑奴聚居地。……这些闪电预告着雷鸣，黑奴们只缺一位足够勇敢的首领，把他们驱向
他在哪里，这位大自然为了人类的荣誉
还欠我们一位的伟人？这位新的斯巴达克斯在哪里？……”

en: In this version of the famous passage, modified in successive editions of the

, the most radical stance is in the unmistakable reference to a single human species. But just as with Las Casas, just as with Buffon or the left of the French Assembly, the practical conclusions from what looks like a revolutionary philosophy are ambiguous. In Diderot-Raynal, as in the few other times it appears in writing, the evocation of a slave rebellion was primarily a rhetorical device. The concrete possibility of such a rebellion flourishing into a revolution and a modern black state was still part of the unthinkable.
zh: 在这一版著名段落中——它在
历次版本中屡经修改——最激进的立场在于对单一人类物种的明确指认。但正如拉斯·卡萨斯的情形，正如布封或法国议会左翼的情形，从看似革命的哲学中得出的实际结论是含混的。在狄德罗—雷纳尔那里，正如在文字中偶尔出现的其他几次一样，对奴隶起义的唤起主要是一种修辞手段。这样一场起义发展成革命并建立一个现代黑人国家的具体可能性，仍属于无法构想之事。

en: Indeed, the political appeal—if appeal there was—is murky. To start with, Diderot’s interlocutors are not the enslaved masses nor even the Spartacus who may or may not rise in an uncertain future. Diderot here is the voice of the enlightened West admonishing its colonialist counterpart.
zh: 的确，其政治诉求——如果确有诉求的话——是模糊的。首先，狄德罗的对话者不是被奴役的群众，甚至也不是那位在不确定的未来中可能崛起也可能不崛起的斯巴达克斯。狄德罗在这里是启蒙西方的声音，训诫它自身殖民主义的那一面。

en: Second and more important, “slavery” was at that time an easy metaphor, accessible to a large public who knew that the word stood for a number of evils except perhaps the evil of itself. Slavery in the parlance of the philosophers could be whatever was wrong with European rule in Europe and elsewhere. To wit, the same Diderot applauded U.S. revolutionaries for having “burned their chains,” for having “refused slavery.” Never mind that some of them owned slaves. The
was also a cry against “slavery.”
Mulatto
from the Caribbean told the French Assembly that their status as second-class free men was equivalent to slavery.

This metaphorical usage permeated the discourse of various nascent disciplines from philosophy to political economy up to Marx and beyond. References to slave resistance must thus be regarded in light of these rhetorical clichés. For if today we can read the successive “Declarations of the Rights of Man” or the U.S. Bill of Rights as naturally including every single human being, it is far from certain that this revisionist reading was the favored interpretation of the “men” of 1789 and 1791.
zh: 其次也更重要的是，“奴隶制”在当时是一个信手拈来的隐喻，广大公众都能领会：这个词代表种种罪恶，唯独也许不代表它本身的罪恶。在哲学家的用语中，奴隶制可以是欧洲统治在欧洲本土及其他地方的一切弊病。譬如，正是这位狄德罗，曾为美国革命者“烧毁了他们的锁链”、“拒绝了奴隶制”而喝彩。至于其中有人自己就拥有奴隶，在这番赞美里倒无关紧要。
也是一声反对“奴隶制”的呐喊。
来自加勒比的穆拉托
告诉法国议会，他们作为二等自由人的地位等同于奴隶制。
这种隐喻用法渗透了从哲学到政治经济学等各种新兴学科的话语，直到马克思及其以后。因此，对奴隶抵抗的提及必须放在这些修辞套话的光照下来看待。因为，如果今天我们可以把历次“人权宣言”或美国《权利法案》读作自然而然地涵盖每一个人，那么远不能确定，这种修正主义的读法就是1789年和1791年的“人们”所偏爱的解释。

en: Third, here as in the rarer texts that speak clearly of the right to insurrection, the possibility of a successful rebellion by slaves or colonized peoples is in a very distant future, still a specter of what might happen if the system remains unchanged.
The implication is, of course, that improvement within the system, or at any rate, starting from the system, could prevent carnage, surely not the philosophers’ favorite outcome.
zh: 第三，在这里，正如在那些更罕见地明确谈论起义权利的文本中一样，奴隶或被殖民人民成功反叛的可能性被置于十分遥远的未来，仍然只是一个幽灵：如果系统保持不变，可能会发生什么。
其言下之意当然是：系统内部的改良，或至少从系统出发的改良，能够避免杀戮——而杀戮肯定不是哲学家们最乐见的结局。

en: Fourth and finally, this was an age of change and inconsistency. Few thinkers had the politics of their philosophy. Radical action on the issue of slavery often came from unsuspected corners, notably in England or in the United States.
After examining the contradictions of the

, Michèle Duchet concludes that the book is politically reformist and philosophically revolutionary. But even the philosophical revolution is not as neat as it first appears, and Duchet admits elsewhere that for Raynal to civilize is to colonize.
zh: 第四也是最后，这是一个变动与不一致的时代。鲜有思想家的政治与其哲学相一致。在奴隶制问题上的激进行动往往来自意想不到的角落，尤其是在英国或美国。
米歇尔·杜歇在考察了
的种种矛盾之后得出结论：这本书在政治上是改良主义的，在哲学上是革命的。但即便是这场哲学革命，也不像初看那样整齐划一；杜歇在别处也承认，对雷纳尔来说，开化就是殖民。

en: Contradictions were plentiful, within philosophy, within politics, and between the two, even within the radical left. They are clearly displayed in the tactics of the pro-mulatto lobby, the Société des Amis des Noirs. The Société’s philosophical point of departure was, of course, the full equality of humankind: some of its founding members participated in drafting the Declaration of Rights of Man. But here again were degrees of humanity. The sole sustained campaign of the self-proclaimed Friends of the Blacks was their effort to guarantee the civil and political rights of free mulatto owners. This emphasis was not simply a tactical maneuver. Many members on the left side of the Assembly went way beyond the call of duty to emphasize that not all blacks were equally worth defending. On December 11, 1791, Grégoire, for instance, denounced the danger of suggesting political rights for black slaves. “To give political rights to men who do not know their duties would be perhaps like placing a sword in the hands of a madman.”
zh: 矛盾大量存在：哲学之内、政治之内、两者之间，甚至激进左翼内部。它们清楚地显示在亲穆拉托游说团体

的策略中。该社的哲学出发点当然是人类的完全平等：它的一些创始成员参与起草了《人权宣言》。但这里又出现了人性的等级。这些自封的黑人之友唯一持续进行的运动，是努力保障拥有财产的自由穆拉托人的公民权与政治权。这一侧重不只是战术动作。议会左翼的许多成员还不厌其烦地强调：并非所有黑人都同样值得捍卫。例如，1791年12月11日，格雷瓜尔谴责了提议给黑人奴隶政治权利的危险。“把政治权利给予不知道自身义务的人，也许无异于把剑放到疯子手里。”

en: Contradictions were no less obvious elsewhere. Under a pseudonym evoking both Judaity and blackness, Condorcet demonstrated all the evils of slavery but then called for
abolition.

Abolitionist Diderot hailed the American Revolution that had retained slavery. Jean-Pierre Brissot asked his friend Jefferson, whose stance on slavery was not questioned in France, to join the Ami des Noirs!

Marat and—to a much lesser extent—Robespierre aside, few leading French revolutionaries recognized the right of white Frenchmen to revolt against colonialism, the same right whose application they admired in British North America.
zh: 矛盾在别处同样明显。孔多塞以一个同时唤起犹太性与黑人性的笔名，揭示了奴隶制的一切罪恶，却随即呼吁
废除奴隶制。
废奴主义者狄德罗欢呼保留了奴隶制的美国革命。让-皮埃尔·布里索邀请他的朋友杰斐逊加入黑人之友社——后者的奴隶制立场在法国从未受到质疑！
除了马拉——以及在远为有限的程度上罗伯斯庇尔——法国大革命领袖中，很少有人承认法国殖民地的白人有权反抗殖民统治。他们却赞赏英属北美的殖民地居民行使同样的权利。
body.review: 底本作 Jean-Pierre Brissot，法国国家图书馆目录署名 Jacques-Pierre Brissot de Warville。第56段同。

en: To sum up, in spite of the philosophical debates, in spite of the rise of abolitionism, the Haitian Revolution was unthinkable in the West not only because it challenged slavery and racism but because of the way it did so. When the insurrection first broke in northern Saint-Domingue, a number of radical writers in Europe and very few in the Americas had been willing to acknowledge, with varying reservations—both practical and philosophical—the humanity of the enslaved. Almost none drew from this acknowledgment the necessity to abolish slavery immediately. Similarly, a handful of writers had evoked intermittently and, most often, metaphorically the possibility of mass resistance among the slaves. Almost none had actually conceded that the slaves could—let alone should—indeed revolt.

Louis Sala-Molins claims that slavery was the ultimate test of the Enlightenment. We can go one step further: The Haitian Revolution was the ultimate test to the universalist pretensions of both the French and the American revolutions. And they both failed.

children: In 1791, there is no public debate on the record, in France, in England, or in the United States on the right of black slaves to achieve self-determination, and the right to do so by way of armed resistance.

zh: 总而言之，尽管有哲学论争，尽管废奴主义兴起，海地革命在西方仍是无法构想的，不仅因为它挑战了奴隶制和种族主义，更因为它挑战的方式。当起义最初在圣多明各北部爆发时，欧洲有一些激进作家、美洲有极少数作家，曾愿意承认被奴役者的人性——尽管带着种种实践上和哲学上的保留。几乎没有人从这一承认中得出必须立即废除奴隶制的结论。同样，少数作家曾断断续续地、而且大多是以隐喻方式，唤起奴隶展开集体抵抗的可能性。几乎没有人真正承认奴隶能够——更不用说应当——确实起义。
路易·萨拉-莫兰声称，奴隶制是启蒙运动的终极检验。我们可以再进一步：海地革命是对法国革命和美国革命双方普遍主义抱负的终极检验。而两者都失败了。

children: 在1791年，无论在法国、英国还是美国，都没有任何记录在案的公开辩论，讨论黑人奴隶实现自决的权利，以及以武装抵抗方式实现自决的权利。

en: Not only was the Revolution unthinkable and, therefore, unannounced in the West, it was also—to a large extent—unspoken among the slaves themselves. By this I mean that the Revolution was not preceded or even accompanied by an explicit intellectual discourse.

One reason is that most slaves were illiterate and the printed word was not a realistic means of propaganda in the context of a slave colony. But another reason is that the claims of the revolution were indeed too radical to be formulated in advance of its deeds. Victorious practice could assert them only after the fact. In that sense, the revolution was indeed at the limits of the thinkable, even in Saint-Domingue, even among the slaves, even among its own leaders.
zh: 这场革命不仅在西方无法构想、因而无人预告，而且在很大程度上，在奴隶自己中间也未被言说。我的意思是，这场革命之前没有、甚至进行之中也没有伴随一种明确的知识话语。
一个原因是大多数奴隶不识字，在奴隶殖民地的语境中，印刷文字不是现实的宣传手段。但另一个原因是，这场革命的主张确实过于激进，无法先于其行动而被表述出来。只能等到行动取胜之后，才有可能申明这些主张。在这个意义上，这场革命确实处于可构想之物的极限，即便在圣多明各，即便在奴隶中间，即便在它自己的领袖中间。

en: We need to recall that the key tenets of the political philosophy that became explicit in Saint-Domingue/Haiti between 1791 and 1804 were not accepted by world public opinion until after World War II. When the Haitian Revolution broke out, only five percent of a world population estimated at nearly 800 million would have been considered “free” by modern standards. The British campaign for abolition of the slave

was in its infancy; the abolition of slavery was even further behind. Claims about the fundamental uniqueness of humankind, claims about the ethical irrelevance of racial categories or of geographical situation to matters of governance and, certainly, claims about the right of

peoples to self-determination went against received wisdom in the Atlantic world and beyond. Each could reveal itself in Saint-Domingue only through practice. By necessity, the Haitian Revolution thought itself out politically and philosophically as it was taking place. Its project, increasingly radicalized throughout thirteen years of combat, was revealed in successive spurts. Between and within its unforeseen stages, discourse always lagged behind practice.
zh: 我们需要回想：1791年至1804年间在圣多明各/海地变得明确的那套政治哲学的关键信条，直到第二次世界大战之后才被世界舆论接受。海地革命爆发时，据估计近八亿的世界人口中，按现代标准只有百分之五可被视为“自由人”。英国废除奴隶
的运动尚处襁褓；废除奴隶制本身更是遥遥落后。关于全人类在根本上同属一体的主张，关于种族范畴或地理位置在伦理上与治理事务无关的主张，当然还有关于
民族都有自决权的主张，都违背了大西洋世界乃至更广范围的通行见解。每一项都只能通过实践在圣多明各显现自身。出于必然，海地革命是在进行之中才在政治上和哲学上把自己想清楚的。它的方案在十三年战斗中日益激进化，在一波接一波的行动中逐渐显露出来。在其无法预见的各阶段之间和各阶段之内，话语总是落后于实践。

en: The Haitian Revolution expressed itself mainly through its deeds, and it is through political practice that it challenged Western philosophy and colonialism. It did produce a few texts whose philosophical import is explicit, from Louverture’s declaration of Camp Turel to the Haitian Act of Independence and the Constitution of 1805. But its intellectual and ideological newness appeared most clearly with each and every political threshold crossed, from the mass insurrection (1791) to the crumbling of the colonial apparatus (1793), from general liberty (1794) to the conquest of the state machinery (1797–98), from Louverture’s taming of that machinery (1801) to the proclamation of Haitian independence with Dessalines (1804). Each and every one of these steps—leading up to and culminating in the emergence of a modern “black state,” still largely part of the unthinkable until the twentieth century—challenged further the ontological order of the West and the global order of colonialism.
zh: 海地革命主要通过其行动表达自身，它正是通过政治实践挑战了西方哲学与殖民主义。它确实产生了少数哲学意涵明确的文本，从卢维杜尔的蒂雷尔营地（Camp Turel）宣言到海地《独立宣言》和1805年宪法。但它的思想与意识形态之新，最清楚地显现在它跨过的每一个政治门槛上：从群众起义（1791）到殖民机器的崩塌（1793），从普遍自由（1794）到对国家机器的夺取（1797–98），从卢维杜尔对那台机器的驯服（1801）到德萨利纳宣告海地独立（1804）。这些步骤中的每一步——层层推进，最终达于一个现代“黑人国家”的诞生，而它直到二十世纪仍大体属于无法构想之事——都进一步挑战了西方的本体论秩序和殖民主义的全球秩序。

en: This also meant that the Haitian revolutionaries were not overly restricted by previous ideological limits set by professional intellectuals in the colony or elsewhere, that they could break new ground—and, indeed, they did so repeatedly. But it further meant that philosophical and political debate in the West, when it occurred, could only be reactive. It dealt with the impossible only after that impossible had become fact; and even then, the facts were not always accepted as such.
zh: 这也意味着，海地革命者并未过分受制于殖民地内或其他地方的职业知识分子先前设定的意识形态界限，他们能够开辟新天地——而且确实一再这样做。但这还意味着，西方的哲学与政治辩论即便发生，也只能是对既成事实的反应。它只有在那不可能之事已成为事实之后才去处理它；而即便那时，事实也未必总被当作事实接受。
