en: Dealing with the Unthinkable: The Failures of Narration
zh: 应对无法构想之事：叙述的种种失败

en: When the news of the massive uprising of August 1791 first hit France, the most common reaction among interested parties was disbelief: the facts were too unlikely; the news had to be false. Only the most vocal representatives of the planter party took them seriously, in part because they were the first to be informed via their British contacts, in part because they had the most to lose if indeed the news was verified. Others, including colored plantation owners then in France and most of the left wing of the French assembly, just could not reconcile their perception of blacks with the idea of a large-scale black rebellion.
In an impassioned speech delivered to the French assembly on 30 October 1791, delegate Jean-Pierre Brissot, a founding member of the

and moderate anti-colonialist, outlined the reasons why the news had to be false: a) anyone who knew the blacks had to realize that it was simply impossible for fifty thousand of them to get together so fast and act in concert; b) slaves could not conceive of rebellion on their own, and mulattoes and whites were not so insane as to incite them to full-scale violence; c) even if the slaves had rebelled in such huge numbers, the superior French troops would have defeated them. Brissot went on:
zh: 当1791年8月大规模起义的消息最初传到法国时，利益相关各方最常见的反应是不信：事实太不可能了；消息一定是假的。只有种植园主党中最直言无忌的代表把它当真，一方面因为他们经由英国关系最先得知消息，另一方面因为一旦消息属实，他们损失最大。其他人——包括当时身在法国的有色人种植园主和法国议会左翼的大部分人——就是无法把他们对黑人的认知与大规模黑人反叛的想法调和起来。
在1791年10月30日向法国议会发表的一篇激昂演说中，代表让-皮埃尔·布里索——
创始成员、温和的反殖民主义者——列举了消息必假的理由：甲）任何了解黑人的人都必须意识到，五万名黑人如此迅速地聚集并协同行动，根本不可能；乙）奴隶自己构想不出反叛，而穆拉托和白人也不至于疯狂到煽动他们全面施暴；丙）即便奴隶以如此庞大的人数反叛，优越的法国军队也会击败他们。布里索接着说：

en: What are 50,000 men, badly armed, undisciplined and used to fear when faced with 1,800 Frenchmen used to fearlessness? What! In 1751, Dupleix and a few hundred Frenchmen could break the siege of Pondichéri and beat a well-equipped army of 100,000 Indians, and M. de Blanchelande with French troops and cannons would fear a much inferior troop of blacks barely armed?
zh: 五万名装备低劣、毫无纪律、习惯于恐惧的人，面对一千八百名一贯无所畏惧的法国人，算得了什么？什么！1751年，迪普莱克斯和几百名法国人就能打破本地治里之围，击败一支装备精良的十万印度大军；而德·布朗什朗德先生带着法国军队和大炮，竟会害怕一支差得远、几乎没武装的黑人队伍？

en: With such statements from a “Friend,” the revolution did not need enemies. Yet so went majority opinion from left to center-right within the Assembly until the news was confirmed beyond doubt. Confirmation did not change the dominant views. When detailed news reached France, many observers were frightened not by the revolt itself but by the fact that the colonists had appealed to the English.

A serious long-term danger coming from the blacks was still unthinkable. Slowly though, the size of the uprising sank in. Yet even then, in France as in Saint-Domingue, as indeed in Jamaica, Cuba, and the United States before, planters, administrators, politicians, or ideologues found explanations that forced the rebellion back within their worldview, shoving the facts into the proper order of discourse. Since blacks could not have generated such a massive endeavor, the insurrection became an unfortunate repercussion of planters’ miscalculations. It did not aim at revolutionary change, given its royalist influences. It was not supported by a majority of the slave population. It was due to outside agitators. It was the unforeseen consequence of various conspiracies connived by non-slaves. Every party chose its favorite enemy as the most likely conspirator behind the slave uprising. Royalist, British, mulatto, or Republican conspirators were seen or heard everywhere by dubious and interested witnesses. Conservative colonialists and anti-slavery republicans accused each other of being the brains behind the revolt. Inferences were drawn from writings that could not have possibly reached or moved the slaves of Saint-Domingue even if they knew how to read. In a revealing speech, deputy Blangilly urged his colleagues to consider the possibility that the rebellion was due, at least in part, to the slaves’ natural desire for freedom—a possibility that most rejected then and later. Blangilly then proceeded to suggest what was in his view the most logical conclusion: a law for the amelioration of slavery.
Legitimate as it was, the slaves’ natural desire for freedom could not be satisfied, lest it threaten France’s interests.
zh: 有了这样一位“朋友”的这番言论，革命都不需要敌人了。然而直到消息被确证无疑之前，议会内从左翼到中右翼的多数意见就是如此。确证并没有改变主流看法。当详细消息传到法国时，许多观察家害怕的不是反叛本身，而是殖民者向英国人求援这件事。

来自黑人的严重长期危险仍是无法构想的。不过慢慢地，起义的规模开始被人接受。但即便那时，在法国和圣多明各——正如先前在牙买加、古巴和美国——种植园主、行政官、政客或意识形态家们找到了种种解释，把反叛强行塞回他们的世界观之内，把事实推入话语的固有秩序。既然黑人不可能发起如此大规模的事业，起义就成了种植园主失算的不幸后果。鉴于其保王党影响，它并不以革命性变革为目标。它没有得到奴隶人口多数的支持。它是外部煽动者所为。它是非奴隶们策划的种种阴谋的意外后果。每一党都挑选自己最中意的敌人，当作奴隶起义背后最可能的阴谋家。可疑而别有用心的见证人到处看见或听见保王党、英国、穆拉托或共和派的阴谋家。保守的殖民主义者和反奴隶制的共和派互相指责对方是反叛的主谋。人们从一些著作中引出推论，而那些著作即便奴隶识字，也不可能传到圣多明各奴隶手中或打动他们。在一篇颇能说明问题的演说中，代表布朗日伊敦促同僚们考虑一种可能性：反叛至少部分源于奴隶对自由的天然渴望——这种可能性当时和后来都被大多数人拒绝。布朗日伊接着提出了他眼中最合逻辑的结论：一部改善奴隶处境的法律。
奴隶对自由的天然渴望尽管正当，却不能被满足，以免威胁法国的利益。

en: For thirteen years at least, Western public opinion pursued this game of hide-and-seek with the news coming out of Saint-Domingue. With every new threshold, the discourse accommodated some of the irrefutable data, questioned others, and provided reassuring explanations for the new package so created. By the spring of 1792, for instance, even the most distant observer could no longer deny the extent of the rebellion, the extraordinary number of slaves and plantations involved, the magnitude of the colonists’ material losses. But then, many even in Saint-Domingue argued that the disaster was temporary, that everything would return to order. Thus, an eyewitness commented: “If the whites and the free mulattoes knew what was good for them, and kept tightly together, it is quite possible that things would return to normal,

children: considering the ascendancy that the white has always had over the negroes.

en: Note the doubt (the witness is tempted to believe his eyes); but note also that the nomenclature has not moved. Worldview wins over the facts: white hegemony is natural and taken for granted; any alternative is still in the domain of the unthinkable. Yet this passage was written in December 1792. At that time, behind the political chaos and the many battles between various armed factions, Toussaint Louverture and his closest followers were building up the avant-garde that would push the revolution to the point of no return. Indeed, six months later, civil commissar Léger Félicité Sonthonax was forced to declare free all slaves willing to fight under the French republican flag. A few weeks after Sonthonax’s proclamation, in August 1793, Toussaint Louverture raised the stakes with his proclamation from Camp Turel: immediate unconditional freedom and equality for all.
zh: 至少十三年间，西方舆论就这样与来自圣多明各的消息玩着捉迷藏。每到一个新门槛，话语就接纳一部分无可辩驳的材料，质疑另一部分，并再把这些材料拼成一套令人安心的解释。例如到1792年春，即便最疏远的观察家也无法再否认反叛的规模、卷入的奴隶与种植园之异乎寻常的数量、殖民者物质损失之惨重。但接着，甚至在圣多明各也有许多人辩称灾难是暂时的，一切都会恢复秩序。于是，一位目击者评论道：“如果白人和自由穆拉托知道什么对自己有利，紧紧抱团，事情很可能恢复正常，

children: 考虑到白人对黑鬼一向拥有的优势。

zh: 注意这里的怀疑（见证人忍不住想相信自己的眼睛）；但也注意命名体系纹丝未动。世界观压过了事实：白人霸权是自然的、理所当然的；任何替代选项仍属于无法构想之域。然而这段话写于1792年12月。那时，在政治混乱和各武装派系间的无数次战斗背后，杜桑·卢维杜尔和他最亲密的追随者正在组建将把革命推过不归点的先锋队。的确，六个月后，民政专员莱热·费利西泰·松托纳被迫宣布：一切愿意在法兰西共和国旗帜下战斗的奴隶均为自由人。松托纳公告几周之后，1793年8月，杜桑·卢维杜尔以蒂雷尔营地公告加码：立即、无条件地给所有人自由与平等。

en: By then, the old conspiracy theories should have become irrelevant. Clearly, the Louverture party was not willing to take orders from colonists, French Jacobins, or agents of foreign powers. What was going on in Saint-Domingue was, by all definitions, the most important slave rebellion ever witnessed and it had developed its own dynamics. Surprisingly, conspiracy theories survived long enough to justify the trials of a few Frenchmen accused to have fomented or helped the rebellion, from Blanchelande, the old royalist governor of 1791, to republican governor Lavaux, to Félicité Sonthonax, the Jacobin.
zh: 到那时，旧的阴谋论本应已不相干。显然，卢维杜尔一党不愿听命于殖民者、法国雅各宾派或外国势力的代理人。圣多明各正在发生的，按任何定义都是有史以来最重要的奴隶反叛，而且它已发展出自己的动力。令人惊讶的是，阴谋论经久不散，以致后来还能被用作审判几名法国人的理由，指控他们煽动或协助反叛：从1791年的老保王党总督布朗什朗德，到共和派总督拉沃，再到雅各宾派费利西泰·松托纳。

en: As the power of Louverture grew, every other party struggled to convince itself and its counterparts that the achievements of the black leadership would ultimately benefit someone else. The new black elite had to be, willingly or not, the pawn of a “major” international power. Or else, the colony would fall apart and a legitimate international state would pick up the pieces. Theories assuming chaos under black leadership continued even after Louverture and his closest lieutenants fully secured the military, political, and civil apparatus of the colony. If some foreign governments—notably the United States—were willing to maintain a guarded collaboration with the Louverture regime, it was in part because they “knew” that an independent state led by former slaves was an impossibility. Toussaint himself may have not believed in the possibility of independence whereas, for all practical purposes, he was ruling Saint-Domingue as if it were independent.
zh: 随着卢维杜尔权力增长，其他每一方都竭力让自己和对方相信：黑人领导层的成就最终会让别的什么人受益。新的黑人精英必定是——无论情愿与否——某个“主要”国际强权的棋子。要不然，殖民地就会分崩离析，由某个在国际上获承认的国家来收拾残局。假定黑人领导下必生混乱的理论，甚至在卢维杜尔及其最亲密的副手已完全掌控殖民地军事、政治和民事机器之后，仍在继续。如果某些外国政府——尤其是美国——愿意与卢维杜尔政权保持谨慎的合作，部分原因在于它们“知道”：一个由前奴隶领导的独立国家是不可能存在的。杜桑自己也许都不相信独立的可能性，尽管就一切实际目的而言，他统治圣多明各已如同它是一个独立国家。

en: Opinion in Saint-Domingue, in North America, and in Europe constantly dragged after the facts. Predictions, when they were made, revealed themselves useless. Once the French expedition of reconquest was launched in 1802, pundits were easily convinced that France would win the war. In England, the
doubted that Toussaint would even oppose a resistance: he was likely to flee the country.

Leclerc himself, the commander of the French forces, predicted in early February that the war would be over in two weeks. He was wrong by two years, give or take two months. Yet planters in Saint-Domingue apparently shared his optimism. Leclerc reported to the Minister of the Marine that French residents were already enjoying the smell of victory. Newspapers in Europe and North and Latin America translated and commented on these dispatches: restoration was near.
zh: 圣多明各、北美和欧洲的舆论总是拖在事实后面。预测一旦作出，就显出其无用。1802年法国再征服远征一经发动，评论家们便轻易相信法国将赢得战争。在英国，
（原文 Cobbet，当作 Cobbett）甚至怀疑杜桑会抵抗：他很可能逃离这个国家。
法军司令勒克莱尔本人在2月初预言战争两周内结束。他错了两年，上下差不超过两个月。然而圣多明各的种植园主显然分享他的乐观。勒克莱尔向海军部长报告说，法国侨民已经在享受胜利的气息。欧洲和南北美洲的报纸翻译并评论这些电讯：复辟在即。

en: By mid-1802, the debacle of Louverture’s army seemed to verify that prophecy. The rejection of the truce by a significant minority of armed rebels—among whom was Sans Souci—and the full-scale resumption of military operations when the war within the war forced the colonial high brass to rejoin the revolution in the fall of 1802 did little to change the dominant views. Despite the alliance between the forces of Dessalines, Pétion, and Christophe and the repeated victories of the new revolutionary army, few outside of Saint-Domingue could foresee the outcome of this Negro rebellion. As late as the fall of 1803, a complete victory by the former slaves and the creation of an independent state was still unthinkable in Europe and North America. Only long after the 1804 declaration of independence would the fait accompli be ungraciously accepted.
zh: 到1802年年中，卢维杜尔军队的溃败似乎印证了那个预言。相当一部分武装反叛者——其中包括桑苏西——拒绝停战；1802年秋，战争中的战争迫使殖民军高层重新加入革命，军事行动全面重启——这些都几乎没有改变主流看法。尽管德萨利纳、佩蒂翁和克里斯托夫的部队结成联盟，尽管新革命军屡获胜利，圣多明各之外几乎没有人能预见这场黑人反叛的结局。直到1803年秋，前奴隶的完全胜利和一个独立国家的建立，在欧洲和北美仍是无法构想之事。只有在1804年独立宣言发表很久之后，这一既成事实（fait accompli）才被不情不愿地接受。

en: Ungraciously, indeed. The international recognition of Haitian independence was even more difficult to gain than military victory over the forces of Napoleon. It took more time and more resources, more than a half century of diplomatic struggles. France imposed a heavy indemnity on the Haitian state in order to formally acknowledge its own defeat. The United States and the Vatican, notably, recognized Haitian independence only in the second half of the nineteenth century.
zh: 的确是不情不愿。海地独立的国际承认，比在军事上战胜拿破仑的军队更难获得。它耗费了更多时间和更多资源——半个多世纪的外交斗争。法国为了正式承认自己的战败，向海地国家强加了一笔沉重的赔款。尤其值得注意的是，美国和梵蒂冈直到十九世纪下半叶才承认海地独立。

en: Diplomatic rejection was only one symptom of an underlying denial. The very deeds of the revolution were incompatible with major tenets of dominant Western ideologies. They remained so until at least the first quarter of this century. Between the Haitian independence and World War I, in spite of the successive abolitions of slavery, little changed within the various ladders that ranked humankind in the minds of the majorities in Europe and the Americas. In fact, some views deteriorated.

The nineteenth century was, in many respects, a century of retreat from some of the debates of the Enlightenment. Scientific racism, a growing but debated strain of Enlightenment thought, gained a much wider audience, further legitimizing the ontological nomenclature inherited from the Renaissance. The carving up of Asia and above all of Africa reinforced both colonial practice and ideology. Thus in most places outside of Haiti, more than a century after it happened, the revolution was still largely unthinkable history.
zh: 外交上的拒绝只是深层否认的一个症状。革命的行动本身与西方主导意识形态的主要信条互不相容。这种不相容至少持续到二十世纪头二十五年。从海地独立到第一次世界大战之间，尽管奴隶制被相继废除，在欧洲和美洲大多数人心目中给人类分等的各种阶梯却几乎没有变化。事实上，有些看法还恶化了。
十九世纪在许多方面是从启蒙运动的某些论争中退却的世纪。科学种族主义——启蒙思想中一支不断壮大但备受争议的脉络——获得了远为广泛的受众，进一步给从文艺复兴继承的本体论分类赋予正当性。对亚洲、尤其是对非洲的瓜分，强化了殖民实践与殖民意识形态。于是，在海地之外的大多数地方，这场革命发生一个多世纪之后，它在很大程度上仍是无法构想的历史。

en: Erasure and Trivialization: Silences in World History
zh: 抹除与琐碎化：世界历史中的沉默

en: I have fleshed out two major points so far. First, the chain of events that constitute the Haitian Revolution was unthinkable before these events happened. Second, as they happened, the successive events within that chain were systematically recast by many participants and observers to fit a world of possibilities. That is, they were made to enter into narratives that made sense to a majority of Western observers and readers. I will now show how the revolution that was thought impossible by its contemporaries has also been silenced by historians. Amazing in this story is the extent to which historians have treated the events of Saint-Domingue in ways quite similar to the reactions of its Western contemporaries. That is, the narratives they build around these facts are strikingly similar to the narratives produced by individuals who thought that such a revolution was impossible.
zh: 到目前为止，我已充实了两个主要论点。第一，构成海地革命的事件链条在这些事件发生之前是无法构想的。第二，随着它们发生，链条中相继发生的事件被许多参与者和观察者系统地重塑，以塞进一个可能性的世界。也就是说，它们被安排进入对大多数西方观察家和读者说得通的叙述。我现在要展示：这场被同时代人认为不可能的革命，如何也被历史学家沉默化了。这个故事中令人惊异的是，历史学家处理圣多明各事件的方式，与其西方同时代人的反应相似到了何种程度。也就是说，他们围绕这些事实构建的叙述，与那些认为这样一场革命不可能的人所生产的叙述，惊人地相似。

en: The treatment of the Haitian Revolution in written history outside of Haiti reveals two families of tropes that are identical, in formal (rhetorical) terms, to figures of discourse of the late eighteenth century. The first kind of tropes are formulas that tend to erase directly the fact of a revolution. I call them, for short, formulas of erasure. The second kind tends to empty a number of singular events of their revolutionary content so that the entire string of facts, gnawed from all sides, becomes trivialized. I call them formulas of banalization. The first kind of tropes characterizes mainly the generalists and the popularizers—textbook authors, for example. The second are the favorite tropes of the specialists. The first type recalls the general silence on resistance in eighteenth-century Europe and North America. The second recalls the explanations of the specialists of the times, overseers and administrators in Saint-Domingue, or politicians in Paris. Both are formulas of silence.
zh: 海地之外成文历史对海地革命的处理，显示出两类修辞格，它们在形式（修辞）层面与十八世纪晚期的话语格完全相同。第一类修辞格是倾向于直接抹除革命这一事实的公式。我简称它们为抹除程式。第二类倾向于抽空一系列单个事件的革命内容，使整串事实被从四面八方啃噬之后变得琐碎。我把这类修辞称作琐碎化程式。第一类修辞格主要是通才作者和普及者——例如教科书作者——的特征。第二类是专家们的最爱。第一类让人想起十八世纪欧洲和北美对抵抗的总体沉默。第二类让人想起当时专家们的解释：圣多明各的监工和行政官，或巴黎的政客。两者都是制造沉默的程式。

en: The literature on slavery in the Americas and on the Holocaust suggests that there may be structural similarities in global silences or, at the very least, that erasure and banalization are not unique to the Haitian Revolution. At the level of generalities, some narratives cancel what happened through direct erasure of facts or their relevance. “It” did not

happen; it was not that bad, or that important. Frontal challenges to the fact of the Holocaust or to the relevance of Afro-American slavery belong to this type: The Germans did not really build gas chambers; slavery also happened to non-blacks. On a seemingly different plane, other narratives sweeten the horror or banalize the uniqueness of a situation by focusing on details: each convoy to Auschwitz can be explained on its own terms; some U.S. slaves were better fed than British workers; some Jews did survive. The joint effect of these two types of formulas is a powerful silencing: whatever has not been cancelled out in the generalities dies in the cumulative irrelevance of a heap of details. This is certainly the case for the Haitian Revolution.
zh: 关于美洲奴隶制和大屠杀的文献提示：全球性的沉默之间可能存在结构上的相似，或者至少，抹除与琐碎化并非海地革命所独有。在概括层面，一些叙述通过直接抹除事实或其相关性来取消发生过的事。“那”没有

发生；它没那么糟，也没那么重要。对大屠杀事实本身、或对美洲非洲裔奴隶制之相关性的正面挑战，就属于这一类：德国人并没有真的建造毒气室；奴隶制也发生在非黑人身上。在看似不同的另一层面，另一些叙述通过聚焦细节来淡化恐怖、把一种独特的处境拆解成琐事：每一趟开往奥斯维辛的列车都可以就其自身情况得到解释；有些美国奴隶吃得比英国工人还好；有些犹太人确实活了下来。这两类程式的合力是一种强大的沉默化：凡未在概括层面被取消的，都死在一堆细节累积起来的无关紧要之中。海地革命的情形无疑正是如此。

en: The general silence that Western historiography has produced around the Haitian Revolution originally stemmed from the incapacity to express the unthinkable, but it was ironically reinforced by the significance of the revolution for its contemporaries and for the generation immediately following. From 1791–1804 to the middle of the century, many Europeans and North Americans came to see that revolution as a litmus test for the black race, certainly for the capacities of all Afro-Americans. As Vastey’s pronouncements on Sans Souci clearly show, Haitians did likewise.

Christophe’s forts and palaces, the military efficiency of the former slaves, the impact of yellow fever on the French troops, and the relative weight of external factors on revolutionary dynamics figured highly in these debates. But if the revolution was significant for Haitians—and especially for the emerging Haitian elites as its self-proclaimed inheritors—to most foreigners it was primarily a lucky argument in a larger issue. Thus apologists and detractors alike, abolitionists and avowed racists, liberal intellectuals, economists, and slave owners used the events of Saint-Domingue to make their case, without regard to Haitian history as such. Haiti mattered to all of them, but only as pretext to talk about something else.
zh: 西方史学围绕海地革命制造的总体沉默，最初源于无法表达无法构想之事，但具有讽刺意味的是，它又被这场革命对其同时代人及紧随其后的一代人所具有的意义加强了。从1791–1804年到十九世纪中叶，许多欧洲人和北美人逐渐把那场革命看作对黑人种族——当然也是对美洲所有非洲裔群体的能力——的一场决定性的检验。正如瓦斯泰关于无忧宫的断言清楚显示的，海地人也同样如此。

克里斯托夫的堡垒与宫殿、前奴隶的军事效能、黄热病对法军的影响、外部因素在革命动力中的相对分量，在这些辩论中都很显眼。但如果说这场革命对海地人——尤其对作为其自封继承者的新兴海地精英——意义重大，那么对大多数外国人来说，它主要是更大议题中一个趁手的论据。于是，辩护者与诋毁者、废奴主义者与公开的种族主义者、自由派知识分子、经济学家和奴隶主，都利用圣多明各的事件来论证自己的主张，而不顾海地历史本身。海地对他们所有人都要紧，但只是作为谈论别的事情的借口。

en: With time, the silencing of the revolution was strengthened by the fate of Haiti itself. Ostracized for the better part of the nineteenth century, the country deteriorated both economically and politically—in part as a result of this ostracism.

As Haiti declined, the reality of the revolution seemed increasingly distant, an improbability which took place in an awkward past and for which no one had a rational explanation. The revolution that was unthinkable became a non-event.
zh: 随着时间推移，对革命的沉默化又被海地自身的命运加强。这个国家在十九世纪的大部分时间里遭到排斥，经济和政治都恶化了——部分正是这种排斥的结果。
随着海地衰落，革命的现实显得越来越遥远，成了一件发生在尴尬过去、无人能给出合理解释的不可思议之事。无法构想的革命变成了非事件。

en: Finally, the silencing of the Haitian Revolution also fit the relegation to an historical backburner of the three themes to which it was linked: racism, slavery, and colonialism. In spite of their importance in the formation of what we now call the West, in spite of sudden outbursts of interest as in the United States in the early 1970s, none of these themes has ever become a central concern of the historiographic tradition in a Western country. In fact, each of them, in turn, experienced repeated periods of silence of unequal duration and intensity in Spain, France, Britain, Portugal, The Netherlands, and the United States. The less colonialism and racism seem important in world history, the less important also the Haitian Revolution.
zh: 最后，对海地革命的沉默化，也契合与它相连的三个主题——种族主义、奴隶制、殖民主义——被搁进历史冷宫的命运。尽管它们在我们今天所称的西方的形成中举足轻重，尽管有过兴趣的突然迸发（如1970年代初的美国），这三个主题没有一个曾成为任何一个西方国家史学传统的核心关切。事实上，它们每一个都在西班牙、法国、英国、葡萄牙、荷兰和美国轮流经历过时长与强度不等的反复沉默期。殖民主义和种族主义在世界历史中显得越不重要，海地革命也就越不重要。

en: Thus not surprisingly, as Western historiographies remain heavily guided by national—if not always nationalist—interests, the silencing of Saint-Domingue/Haiti continues in historical writings otherwise considered as models of the genre. The silence is also reproduced in the textbooks and popular writings that are the prime sources on global history for the literate masses in Europe, in the Americas, and in large chunks of the Third World. This corpus has taught generations of readers that the period from 1776 to 1843 should properly be called “The Age of Revolutions.” At the very same time, this corpus has remained silent on the most radical political revolution of that age.
zh: 因此毫不奇怪，由于西方各国史学仍深受各自国家利益的左右，尽管未必奉行民族主义，对圣多明各/海地的沉默化，在那些在其他方面被视为史学典范的著作中继续着。这种沉默也在教科书和通俗读物中再生产，而这些正是欧洲、美洲以及第三世界大片地区识字大众获取全球历史知识的首要来源。这套文献教会了几代读者：1776年至1843年这段时期理应被称为“革命的时代”。而与此同时，这套文献对那个时代最激进的政治革命始终缄口不言。

en: In the United States, for example, with the notable exceptions of Henry Adams and W. E. B. Du Bois, few major writers conceded any significance to the Haitian Revolution in their historical writings up to the 1970s. Very few textbooks even mentioned it. When they did, they made of it a “revolt,” a “rebellion.” The ongoing silence of most Latin-American textbooks is still more tragic. Likewise, historians of Poland have paid little attention to the five thousand Poles involved in the Saint-Domingue campaigns. The silence also persists in England in spite of the fact that the British lost upward of sixty thousand men in eight years in an anti-French Caribbean campaign of which Saint-Domingue was the most coveted prize. The Haitian Revolution appears obliquely as part of
history. The victor is disease, not the Haitians. The Penguin

, a mass circulation pocket encyclopedia that covers the period from 1789 to 1945, has neither Saint-Domingue nor Haiti in its entries. Likewise, historian Eric Hobsbawm, one of the best analysts of this era, managed to write a book entitled
, in which the Haitian Revolution scarcely appears. That Hobsbawm and the editors of the

would probably locate themselves quite differently within England’s political spectrum is one indication that historical silences do not simply reproduce the overt political positions of the historians involved. What we are observing here is archival power at its strongest, the power to define what is and what is not a serious object of research and, therefore, of mention.
zh: 例如在美国，除了亨利·亚当斯和 W. E. B. 杜波依斯这两个显著例外，直到1970年代，重要作家中鲜有人在其历史著作中承认海地革命有任何意义。极少有教科书提到它。即便提到，也把它写成一场“暴动”、一场“叛乱”。大多数拉丁美洲教科书持续的沉默更为可悲。同样，波兰的历史学家很少关注卷入圣多明各战役的五千名波兰人。沉默在英国也持续着，尽管英国人在一场以圣多明各为最想夺取的目标的加勒比对法战事中，八年间损失了六万多人。海地革命只是作为
史的一部分被间接提到。胜利者是疾病，不是海地人。企鹅
——一本覆盖1789年至1945年、发行量巨大的袖珍百科——词条中既没有圣多明各也没有海地。同样，历史学家埃里克·霍布斯鲍姆，这个时代最好的分析者之一，居然写出了一本名为
（原文如此；实际书名为 The Age of Revolution: 1789–1848）的书，其中海地革命几乎不出现。霍布斯鲍姆和《词典》的编者们在英国政治光谱上的自我定位很可能相当不同，这是一个迹象，表明历史沉默并不只是再生产相关历史学家公开的政治立场。我们在这里观察到的，是档案权力最强的形态：定义什么是、什么不是严肃研究对象——因而也是值得提及之物——的权力。

en: The secondary role of conscious ideology and the power of the historical guild to decide relevance become obvious when we consider the case of France. France was the Western country most directly involved in the Haitian Revolution. France fought hard to keep Saint-Domingue and paid a heavy price for it. Napoleon lost nineteen French generals in Saint-Domingue, including his brother-in-law. France lost more men in Saint-Domingue than at Waterloo—as did England.

And although France recovered economically from the loss of Saint-Domingue, it had indeed surrendered the control of its most valuable colony to a black army and that loss had ended the dream of a French empire on the American mainland. The Haitian Revolution prompted the Louisiana Purchase. One would expect such “facts,” none of which is controversial, to generate a chain of mentions, even if negative. Yet a perusal of French historical writings reveals multiple layers of silences.
zh: 当我们考察法国的情形时，自觉意识形态的次要角色、以及历史行会裁定相关性的权力，就变得明显了。法国是最直接卷入海地革命的西方国家。法国为保住圣多明各苦战，并付出了沉重代价。拿破仑在圣多明各损失了十九名法国将军，包括他的妹夫。法国在圣多明各损失的人比在滑铁卢还多——英国也是如此。
而且，尽管法国在经济上从失去圣多明各中恢复了过来，它确实把最有价值的殖民地的控制权拱手让给了一支黑人军队，而这一损失终结了法兰西帝国在美洲大陆的梦想。海地革命促成了路易斯安那购地。人们会指望这样的“事实”——其中没有一条有争议——引发一连串提及，哪怕是负面的提及。然而翻阅法国的历史著作，看到的却是层层沉默。

en: The silencing starts with revolutionary France itself and is linked to a more general silencing of French colonialism. Although by the 1780s France was less involved than Britain in the slave trade, both slavery and colonialism were crucial to the French economy in the second half of the eighteenth century.

Historians debate only the extent—rather than the fact—of France’s dependence on its Caribbean slave territories. All concur that Saint-Domingue was, at the time of its Revolution, the most valuable colony of the Western world and France’s most important possession.

Many contemporaries would have agreed. Whenever the colonial issue was evoked, for instance in the assemblies, it was almost always mingled with Afro-American slavery and both were presented—most often, but not only, by the colonists—as a matter of vital importance for the future of France.
zh: 沉默化始于革命法国本身，并与对法国殖民主义更总体的沉默化相连。尽管到1780年代法国卷入奴隶贸易的程度已不如英国，奴隶制和殖民主义在十八世纪下半叶对法国经济都至关重要。
历史学家争论的只是法国对其加勒比奴隶领地依赖的程度——而非这一事实本身。所有人都同意：圣多明各在其革命之时，是西方世界最有价值的殖民地，是法国最重要的属地。
许多同时代人也会同意。每当殖民问题被提起——例如在各议会中——它几乎总是与美洲非洲裔奴隶制纠缠在一起，而两者都被——最常是、但不限于殖民者——表述为关乎法国未来的头等大事。

en: Even if one leaves room, as one should, for rhetorical hyperbole, the fact that such rhetoric could be deployed is itself telling. But then, we discover a paradox. Every time the revolutionary assemblies, the polemists, journalists, and politicians that helped decide the fate of France between the outbreak of the French Revolution and the independence of Haiti evoked racism, slavery, and colonialism, they explicitly presented these issues as some of the most important questions that France faced, either on moral or on economic grounds. Yet the number of times they debated those same issues was strikingly limited. Considering both the weight of the colonies in French economic life and the heat of the rhetoric involved, the public debate was of short range. The number of individuals involved, the fact that most came from the elites, the limited amount of time that most participants devoted to these issues do not reflect the central place of colonialism in France’s objective existence. They certainly do not reflect either the colonists’ claim that the economic future of the country, or the

claim that the moral present of the nation was at stake. Recent research, including two important books by Yves Benot on colonialism and the French Revolution, has not challenged Daniel Resnick’s earlier judgment that slavery was, even for France’s libertarians, “a derivative concern.”
zh: 即便人们像应该做的那样，为修辞夸张留出余地，这种修辞能够被施展出来这一事实本身就很说明问题。但接着，我们发现一个悖论。从法国大革命爆发到海地独立之间，那些帮助决定法国命运的革命议会、论战家、记者和政客，每次提起种族主义、奴隶制和殖民主义时，都明确地把这些问题表述为法国面临的最重要问题之列——无论基于道德还是经济理由。然而他们辩论这些相同问题的次数却少得惊人。考虑到殖民地在法国经济生活中的分量，以及所涉修辞的热度，实际的公共辩论范围很窄。卷入的人数、多数人来自精英阶层这一事实、多数参与者投入这些问题的有限时间，都不反映殖民主义在法国客观存在中的核心位置。它们当然也不反映殖民者的主张——国家的经济未来危在旦夕，或
的主张——法国眼下的道德处境岌岌可危。晚近的研究，包括伊夫·贝诺关于殖民主义与法国大革命的两本重要著作，都没有推翻丹尼尔·雷斯尼克早先的判断：奴隶制即便对法国的自由倡导者来说，也只是“从其他关切派生出来的问题”。

en: Still, revolutionary France left a trail of records on these subjects. Colonial management and both private and public communications between France and the Americas also left their paper trail. In short, the inaccessibility of sources is only relative. It cannot explain the massive disregard that French historiography shows for the colonial question and, by extension, for the Haitian Revolution. In fact, French historians continue to neglect the colonial question, slavery, resistance, and racism more than the revolutionary assemblies ever did. Most historians ignored or simply skipped whatever record there was. A few took the time for short and often derogatory passages on the Haitian revolutionaries before moving, as it were, to more important subjects.
zh: 尽管如此，革命法国在这些主题上留下了记录的踪迹。殖民管理，以及法国与美洲之间的私人和公共通信，也留下了纸面痕迹。简言之，史料的难以获取只是相对的。它无法解释法国史学对殖民问题——进而对海地革命——表现出的大规模漠视。事实上，法国历史学家对殖民问题、奴隶制、抵抗和种族主义的忽视，至今超过革命议会当年的程度。大多数历史学家无视或干脆跳过了现存的一切记录。少数人花时间写了几段简短、往往带贬损意味的文字谈论海地革命者，然后便转向——可以这么说——更要紧的主题。

en: The list of writers guilty of this silencing includes names attached to various eras, historical schools, and ideological positions, from Mme. de Staël, Alexis de Tocqueville, Adolphe Thiers, Alphonse de Lamartine, Jules Michelet, Albert Mathiez, and André Guérin, to Albert Soboul. Besides minor—and debatable—exceptions in the writings of Ernest Lavisse and, most especially Jean Jaurès, the silencing continues.
Larousse’s glossy compilation of

children: The Great Events of World History

en: , meant to duplicate—and, one supposes, fashion—“the memory of humankind” produces a more polished silence than the Penguin pocket dictionary. It not only skips the Haitian Revolution; it attributes very little space to either slavery or colonialism.

Even the centennial celebrations of French slave emancipation in the 1948 did not stimulate a substantial literature on the subject. More surprising, neither the translation in French of C. L. R. James’s
nor the publication of Aimé Césaire’s
, which both place colonialism and the Haitian Revolution as a central question of the French Revolution, activated French scholarship.
zh: 参与制造这种沉默的作者，涵盖属于各个时代、各个史学流派和各种意识形态立场的名字：从斯塔尔夫人、阿列克西·德·托克维尔、阿道夫·梯也尔、阿尔方斯·德·拉马丁、儒勒·米什莱、阿尔贝·马蒂埃、安德烈·盖兰，到阿尔贝·索布尔。除了埃内斯特·拉维斯、尤其是让·饶勒斯著作中次要的——且有争议的——例外，沉默化在继续。
拉鲁斯那套精美的
汇编，旨在复制——并且人们可以推想，塑造——“人类的记忆”，它生产的沉默比企鹅袖珍词典更加光鲜。它不仅跳过海地革命；给奴隶制和殖民主义的空间也极少。
甚至1948年法国奴隶解放百年庆典，也没有激发出关于这一主题的实质性文献。更令人惊讶的是，无论是 C. L. R. 詹姆斯
的法译本，还是艾梅·塞泽尔
的出版——两者都把殖民主义和海地革命置于法国革命的核心问题位置——都没有激活法国学界。

en: The public celebrations and the flood of publications that accompanied the Bicentennial of the French Revolution in 1989–1991 actively renewed the silence. Massive compilations of five hundred to a thousand pages on revolutionary France, published in the 1980s and directed by France’s most prominent historians, show near total neglect both for colonial issues and the colonial revolution that forcibly brought them to the French estates. Sala-Molins describes and decries the near total erasure of Haiti, slavery, and colonization by French officials and the general public during ceremonies surrounding the Bicentennial.
zh: 1989–1991年法国大革命二百周年期间的公共庆典和出版物洪流，积极地更新了沉默。1980年代出版、由法国最显赫的历史学家主持的五百至一千页的革命法国大型汇编，对殖民问题、以及迫使法国的议事机构面对这些问题的那场殖民地革命，都表现出近乎全盘的漠视。萨拉-莫兰描述并谴责了二百周年庆典期间，法国官员和公众对海地、奴隶制和殖民的近乎全盘的抹除。

en: As this general silencing goes on, increased specialization within the historical guild leads to a second trend. Saint-Domingue/Haiti emerges at the intersection of various interests: colonial history, Caribbean or Afro-American history, the history of slavery, the history of New World peasantries. In any one of these subfields, it has now become impossible to silence the fact that a revolution took place. Indeed, the revolution itself, or even series of facts within it, have become legitimate topics for serious research within any of these subfields.
zh: 随着这种总体沉默化的继续，历史行会内部日益加深的专业化导致了第二个趋势。圣多明各/海地出现在各个研究领域的交汇处上：殖民史、加勒比史或美洲非洲裔史、奴隶制史、新世界农民史。在这些子领域中的任何一个里，如今都已不可能沉默化一场革命发生过这一事实。的确，革命本身、甚至其中的一系列事实，已成为这些子领域中任何一个里严肃研究的正当课题。

en: How interesting then, that many of the rhetorical figures used to interpret the mass of evidence accumulated by modern historians recall tropes honed by planters, politicians, and administrators both before and during the revolutionary struggle. Examples are plentiful, and I will only cite a few. Many analyses of marronage (“desertion” some still would say) come quite close to the biophysiological explanations preferred by plantation managers.

I have already sketched the pattern: slave A escaped because she was hungry, slave B because she was mistreated.… Similarly, conspiracy theories still provide many historians with a deus ex machina for the events of 1791 and beyond, just as in the rhetoric of the assemblymen of the times. The uprising must have been “prompted,” “provoked,” or “suggested” by some higher being than the slaves themselves: royalists, mulattoes, or other external agents.
zh: 那么，多么有趣：用来解释现代历史学家积累的大量证据的许多修辞格，让人想起种植园主、政客和行政官在革命斗争之前和之中打磨出来的转义。例子很多，我只举几个。许多关于马龙逃亡（marronage，有人仍会说“开小差”）的分析，相当接近种植园管理者偏爱的生物生理解释。
我已勾勒过这个模式：奴隶甲逃跑因为她饿了，奴隶乙因为她受了虐待。……同样，阴谋论仍为许多历史学家提供1791年及此后事件的机械降神（deus ex machina），正如当年议员们的修辞一样。起义必定是由某些被视为比奴隶更有能耐的人“促成”“挑起”或“授意”的：保王党、穆拉托或其他外部代理人。

en: The search for external influences on the Haitian Revolution provides a fascinating example of archival power at work, not because such influences are impossible but because of the way the same historians treat contrary evidence that displays the internal dynamics of the revolution. Thus, many historians are more willing to accept the idea that slaves could have been influenced by whites or free mulattoes, with whom we know they had limited contacts, than they are willing to accept the idea that slaves could have convinced other slaves that they had the right to revolt. The existence of extended communication networks among slaves, of which we have only a glimpse, has not been a “serious” subject of historical research.
zh: 寻找海地革命的外部影响，提供了档案权力运作的一个迷人例证——不是因为这种影响不可能存在，而是因为同一批历史学家对待相反证据的方式，那些证据显示的是革命的内部动力。于是，许多历史学家更愿意接受奴隶可能受白人或者自由穆拉托影响的想法——我们知道奴隶与他们的接触有限——却不愿接受奴隶可能说服其他奴隶相信自己有权起义的想法。奴隶之间存在广泛的联络网络，我们对此只瞥见一斑，而它的存在从未成为历史研究的“严肃”课题。

en: Similarly, historians otherwise eager to find evidence of “external” participation in the 1791 uprising skip the unmistakable evidence that the rebellious slaves had their own program. In one of their earliest negotiations with representatives of the French government, the leaders of the rebellion did not ask for an abstractly couched “freedom.” Rather, their most sweeping demands included three days a week to work on their own gardens and the elimination of the whip. These were not Jacobinist demands adapted to the tropics, nor royalist claims twice creolized. These were slave demands with the strong peasant touch that would characterize independent Haiti. But such evidence of an internal drive, although known to most historians, is not debated—not even to be rejected or interpreted otherwise. It is simply ignored, and this ignorance produces a silence of trivialization.
zh: 同样，那些在其他方面急于寻找1791年起义中“外部”参与证据的历史学家，跳过了确凿无疑的证据：反叛奴隶有自己的纲领。在与法国政府代表最早的一次谈判中，起义领袖们要求的不是抽象措辞的“自由”。毋宁说，他们最全面的要求包括每周三天耕种自己的园地，以及废除鞭刑。这不是适应热带的雅各宾派要求，也不是两度克里奥尔化的保王党主张。这是奴隶的要求，带着将成为独立海地特征的浓厚农民色彩。但这种内部驱动的证据，尽管大多数历史学家都知道，却未被讨论——甚至未被拒绝或作别样解释。它只是被无视，而这种无视生产了一种琐碎化的沉默。

en: In that same vein, historian Robert Stein places most of the credit for the 1793 liberation of the slaves on Sonthonax. The commissar was a zealous Jacobin, a revolutionary in his own right, indeed perhaps the only white man to have evoked concretely and with sympathy the possibility of an armed insurrection among Caribbean slaves both
and in a public forum.

We have no way to estimate the probable course of the Revolution without his invaluable contribution to the cause of freedom. But the point is not empirical. The point is that Stein’s rhetoric echoes the very rhetoric first laid out in Sonthonax’s trial. Implicit in that rhetoric is the assumption that the French connection is both sufficient and necessary to the Haitian Revolution. That assumption trivializes the slaves’ independent sense of their right to freedom and the right to achieve this freedom by force of arms. Other writers tend to stay prudently away from the word “revolution,” more often using such words as “insurgents,” “rebels,” “bands,” and “insurrection.” Behind this terminological fuzziness, these empirical blanks and these preferences in interpretation is the lingering impossibility, which goes back to the eighteenth century, of considering the former slaves as the main actors in the chain of events described.
zh: 循着同样的路数，历史学家罗伯特·斯坦把1793年奴隶解放的大部分功劳归于松托纳。这位专员是热忱的雅各宾派，凭其自身就是革命者，的确也许是唯一一位既
又在公共论坛上，具体而带着同情唤起加勒比奴隶武装起义可能性的白人。

没有他对自由事业的宝贵贡献，革命可能走什么进程，我们无从估计。但要点不在经验层面。要点在于：斯坦的修辞呼应了最初在松托纳审判中铺陈的那套修辞。那套修辞隐含的假定是：与法国的关联是海地革命的充分必要条件。这一假定把奴隶自己认识到有权获得自由、有权以武力争取自由这件事贬成了无足轻重的细节。其他作家倾向于谨慎地避开“革命”一词，更常用“起事者”、“反叛者”、“团伙”、“暴动”这类词。在这种术语的模糊、这些经验空白和这些解释偏好背后，是一种可追溯到十八世纪、挥之不去的不可能性：无法把前奴隶视为所描述事件链条中的主要行动者。

en: Yet since at least the first publication of C. L. R. James’s classic,

(but note the title), the demonstration has been well made to the guild that the Haitian Revolution is indeed a “revolution” in its own right by any definition of the word, and not an appendix of Bastille Day. But only with the popular reedition of James’s book in 1962 and the civil rights movement in the United States did an international counter-discourse emerge, which fed on the historiography produced in Haiti since the nineteenth century. That counter-discourse was revitalized in the 1980s with the contributions of historians whose specialty was neither Haiti nor the Caribbean. Then, Eugene Genovese and—later—Robin Blackburn, echoing Henry Adams and W. E. B. Du Bois, insisted on the central role of the Haitian Revolution in the collapse of the entire system of slavery.
The impact of this counter-discourse remains limited, however, especially since Haitian researchers are increasingly distant from these international debates.
zh: 然而，至少自 C. L. R. 詹姆斯的经典

初版以来（但请注意书名），已向行会充分证明：按这个词的任何定义，海地革命凭其自身就是一场“革命”，而不是攻占巴士底狱的一则附记。但直到1962年詹姆斯著作的通俗再版和美国民权运动，一种国际性的反话语才出现，它以十九世纪以来海地生产的史学为养料。这种反话语在1980年代因一些专长既非海地也非加勒比的历史学家的贡献而重获活力。接着，尤金·吉诺维斯——以及后来的罗宾·布莱克本，呼应亨利·亚当斯和 W. E. B. 杜波依斯——坚持海地革命在整个奴隶制体系崩溃中的核心作用。
然而，这种反话语的影响仍然有限，尤其因为海地研究者与这些国际辩论日益疏远。

en: Thus, the historiography of the Haitian Revolution now finds itself marred by two unfortunate tendencies. On the one hand, most of the literature produced in Haiti remains respectful—too respectful, I would say—of the revolutionary leaders who led the masses of former slaves to freedom and independence. Since the early nineteenth century, the Haitian elites have chosen to respond to racist denigration with an epic discourse lauding

revolution. The epic of 1791–1804 nurtures among them a positive image of blackness quite useful in a white-dominated world. But the epic is equally useful on the home front. It is one of the rare historical alibis of these elites, an indispensable reference to their claims to power.
zh: 于是，海地革命的史学如今发现自己被两种不幸的倾向损害。一方面，海地生产的大部分文献，对带领前奴隶群众走向自由与独立的革命领袖们仍然恭敬——我要说，过于恭敬。自十九世纪初以来，海地精英选择用一种颂扬
革命的史诗话语，来回应种族主义的贬损。1791–1804年的史诗在他们中间培育了一种黑人身份的正面形象，这在白人主导的世界里相当有用。但史诗在国内战线同样有用。它是这些精英少有的历史托词之一，是他们权力主张不可或缺的参照。

en: The empirical value of this epic tradition has steadily declined after its spectacular launching by such nineteenth-century giants as Thomas Madiou and Beaubrun Ardouin, and in spite of individual achievements of the early twentieth century. Unequal access to archives—products and symbols of neo-colonial domination—and the secondary role of empirical precision in this epic discourse continue to handicap Haitian researchers. They excel at putting facts into perspective, but their facts are weak, sometimes wrong, especially since the Duvalier regime explicitly politicized historical discourse.
zh: 这一史诗传统在十九世纪托马·马迪乌和博布伦·阿尔杜安这样的巨匠手中辉煌开场之后，尽管二十世纪早期有个别成就，其经验价值却稳步下降。对档案的不平等获取——档案是新殖民支配的产物与象征——以及经验精确性在这套史诗话语中的次要地位，继续束缚着海地研究者。他们擅长把史实放回更大的历史脉络里，却常缺乏扎实的事实依据，有时所述事实也有误，尤其自杜瓦利埃政权明确把历史话语政治化以来。

en: On the other hand, the history produced outside of Haiti is increasingly sophisticated and rich empirically. Yet its vocabulary and often its entire discursive framework recall frighteningly those of the eighteenth century. Papers and monographs take the tone of plantation records. Analyses of the revolution recall the letters of a La Barre, the pamphlets of French politicians, the messages of Leclerc to Bonaparte or, at best, the speech of Blangilly. I am quite willing to concede that the conscious political motives are not the same. Indeed again, that is part of my point. Effective silencing does not require a conspiracy, not even a political consensus. Its roots are structural. Beyond a stated—and most often sincere—political generosity, best described in U.S. parlance within a liberal continuum, the narrative structures of Western historiography have not broken with the ontological order of the Renaissance. This exercise of power is much more important than the alleged conservative or liberal adherence of the historians involved.
zh: 另一方面，海地之外生产的历史在经验上日益精致而丰富。然而它的词汇、往往还有它的整个话语框架，令人恐惧地让人想起十八世纪。论文和专著带着种植园记录的腔调。对革命的分析让人想起拉巴尔的信、法国政客的小册子、勒克莱尔致波拿巴的电文，或者至多布朗日伊的演说。我很愿意承认，自觉的政治动机并不相同。的确，这再一次正是我的论点的一部分。有效的沉默化不需要阴谋，甚至不需要政治共识。它的根子是结构性的。透过他们公开表明、且往往真诚的宽容政治立场（用美国术语说，大体在自由派的光谱之内），西方史学的叙述结构并未与文艺复兴的本体论秩序决裂。这种权力的行使，比相关历史学家据称的保守派或自由派归属重要得多。

en: The solution may be for the two historiographic traditions—that of Haiti and that of the “foreign” specialists—to merge or to generate a new perspective that encompasses the best of each. There are indications of a move in this direction and some recent works suggest that it may become possible, sometime in the future, to write the history of the revolution that was, for long, unthinkable.
zh: 解决办法也许是让两种史学传统——海地的与“外国”专家的——融合，或生成一种兼收两者之长的新视角。已有迹象表明朝这个方向的移动，一些晚近著作提示：在将来的某个时候，书写这场长期无法构想的革命的历史，也许会成为可能。

en: But what I have said of the guild’s reception of

, of colonial history in France, and of slavery in U.S. history suggests also that neither a single great book nor even a substantial increase in slave resistance studies will fully uncover the silence that surrounds the Haitian Revolution. For the silencing of that revolution has less to do with Haiti or slavery than it has to do with the West.
zh: 但我关于行会如何接受
、关于法国的殖民史、关于美国历史中的奴隶制所说的，也提示：无论一本伟大的书，还是奴隶抵抗研究的大幅增加，都不会彻底揭开围绕海地革命的沉默。因为对那场革命的沉默化，与其说与海地或奴隶制有关，不如说与西方有关。

en: Here again, what is at stake is the interplay between historicity 1 and historicity 2, between what happened and that which is said to have happened. What happened in Haiti between 1791 and 1804 contradicted much of what happened elsewhere in the world before and since. That fact itself is not surprising: the historical process is always messy, often enough contradictory. But what happened in Haiti also contradicted most of what the West has told both itself and others about itself. The world of the West basks in what François Furet calls the second illusion of truth: what happened is what must have happened. How many of us can think of any non-European population without the background of a global domination that now looks preordained? And how can Haiti, or slavery, or racism be more than distracting footnotes within that narrative order?
zh: 这里再一次，利害攸关的是历史性1与历史性2之间的相互作用，是发生过的事情与被说成发生过的事情之间的相互作用。1791年至1804年间海地发生的事，与世界其他地方在此之前和之后发生的许多事相矛盾。这一事实本身并不令人惊讶：历史过程总是杂乱的，往往充满矛盾。但海地发生的事，还与西方讲给自己、也讲给别人听的许多关于自身的叙述相矛盾。西方的世界沐浴在弗朗索瓦·傅勒所说的第二种真理幻觉之中：发生的事就是必定会发生的事。我们中有多少人能在想到任何非欧洲人群时，不带上一幅如今看来命中注定的全球支配的背景？而在那种叙述秩序之内，海地、奴隶制或种族主义，又怎能不只是令人分神的脚注？

en: The silencing of the Haitian Revolution is only a chapter within a narrative of global domination. It is part of the history of the West and it is likely to persist, even in attenuated form, as long as the history of the West is not retold in ways that bring forward the perspective of the world. Unfortunately, we are not even close to such fundamental rewriting of world history, in spite of a few spectacular achievements.
The next chapter goes more directly, albeit from a quite unique angle, into this narrative of global domination which starts in Spain—or is it Portugal?—at the end of the fifteenth century.
zh: 对海地革命的沉默化，只是全球支配叙述中的一个章节。它是西方历史的一部分，而且只要西方的历史不以凸显世界视角的方式重述，它就很可能持续下去，哪怕以减弱的形式。不幸的是，尽管有几项辉煌的成就，我们离这种对世界历史的根本重写还差得很远。
下一章将更直接地——尽管是从一个相当独特的角度——进入这套全球支配的叙述；它始于十五世纪末的西班牙——还是葡萄牙？

en: To be sure, there were oral and written texts of which the philosophical import became increasingly explicit as the Revolution advanced, from the speeches reportedly given at the gatherings that preceded the insurrection to the Haitian Constitution of 1805. But these are primarily political texts marking immediate goals or recent victories. Up to the first post-independence writings of Boisrond-Tonnere, there were no full-time intellectuals to engage in speech acts one step removed from the political battles, as in the French and the American revolutions, the later anticolonial struggles of Latin America, Asia, or Africa, or the revolutions that claimed a Marxist ancestry.

(Port-au-Prince: Imprimerie Henri Deschamps, 1985). Fick remains much too close to the epic rhetoric of the Haitian tradition. Her treatment of resistance is overly ideological and skews her reading of the evidence in the direction of heroism. Nevertheless, her book adds more to the empirical bank on Saint-Domingue than most recent works in the epic tradition. David Geggus’s ongoing research remains empirically impeccable. One wishes that it would continue to move further away from the discourse of banalization and would spell out explicitly, one day, some of its hidden assumptions. The work by the Auguste brothers on the French expedition comes closer to finding a tone that treats its material with ideological respect without falling into a celebration or extrapolating from the evidence. It is well grounded into archival research, yet it does not make concessions to the banalizing discourse.
